scenario: Mac set to Russian, German or Ukrainian: Screenshot.app saves 'Снимок экрана 2026-10-11 в 15.04.05.png' (or 'Bildschirmfoto ...', 'Знімок екрана ...') to the capture folder, user opens the Shelf.
expected: The still is offered as a new card, as an English-named one would be. Movies and stills both arrive whatever the system language.
actual_by_code: Stills are accepted only if the filename starts with a prefix from capturePrefixes() (RecordingPickup.swift:109-122, isCapture :95-104). The 'localized' prefix is read from Bundle(identifier: "com.apple.ScreenCaptureKit") key "Screenshot" (:116). On this macOS 27.0.1 that framework's Localizable.loctable has 43 languages and no key containing 'Screenshot', so the lookup returns the key itself ("Screenshot", already in the list). The real localized word lives in screencaptureui.app Localizable.loctable ('Screenshot' -> 'Снимок экрана' ru, 'Bildschirmfoto' de, 'Знімок екрана' uk). Result: no localized prefix is ever added; localized stills are silently never picked up (movies still arrive because they are matched by type, :96).
existing_test: RecordingPickupTests (no test uses a non-English prefix; testALockScreenScreenshotIsACapture only covers LWScreenShot)

scenario: macOS 27 (this Mac is 27.0.1) enforces pasteboard privacy for programmatic reads (NSPasteboard.accessBehavior): Isla polls the general pasteboard every 0.5 s and reads contents with no user gesture.
expected: Either the read is allowed, or Isla detects the restricted/denied state and says so in Settings instead of silently recording nothing or raising a prompt on every copy.
actual_by_code: ClipboardStore.pollNow (ClipboardStore.swift:174) reads changeCount then calls readObjects/data/string(forType:) (:215, :337) with no accessBehavior, detectPatterns or denial handling anywhere in Sources (grep empty). docs/research/technical-feasibility.md:69 records the risk as 'not active by default as of macOS 26.4' and calls it live forward-looking. Whether 27.0.1 changed that is not in the repo; the clipboard tab and the screenshot-to-Shelf path both depend on these reads.

scenario: First lock on a macOS release whose SkyLight symbols still resolve but whose signatures changed (macOS 27 is installed here).
expected: A missing or changed SPI degrades to 'pill hidden while locked' with no crash, as the code comment promises.
actual_by_code: LockScreenPresence.swift:159-190 resolves eight SLS* symbols with dlsym and unsafeBitCast's them to hard-coded C signatures (:166); only symbol presence is checked. A python ctypes probe on this Mac shows all eight SLS symbols and all seven MediaRemote symbols present on 27.0.1, so the 'missing symbol' fallback will not engage; a changed argument list (SLSSpaceAddWindowsAndRemoveFromSpaces takes a flags int 7, :187) would be undefined behaviour at the first lock, not a graceful hide. Presence is verified; ABI is not.

scenario: Mac sleeps (lid closed) while a track is 'playing' and the player still reports playing with its pre-sleep MediaRemote timestamp after wake (browser tab, Spotify before it republishes).
expected: The bar and lyric resume where the audio actually is; hours of sleep are not added to the track position.
actual_by_code: reportedPosition ages every playing snapshot by wall time: since = Date().timeIntervalSince(takenAt) (MediaController.swift:1887), takenAt being the player's own wall-clock timestamp (helper.m:274-277 -> NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:32). Only a negative age is guarded (:1889); aged is capped at duration (:1893), never at a sane gap. After an 8 h sleep with an unrefreshed timestamp the reading is duration: adopt() takes a forward jump (forwardTolerance) so the bar and lyric snap to the last line until a corroborated rewind lands 2-4 s later. The monotonic anchor (:124) protects the ticker but not this ingest path.

scenario: Mac clock was wrong (ahead) when the Spotify token was issued, then corrected (NTP, manual, VM resume), or the user revokes Isla in Spotify's account page.
expected: A 401 from the Web API forces one token refresh; the heart works again within a request or two.
actual_by_code: Expiry is stored in wall time (SpotifyAccount.swift:270, now+expires_in-60) and trusted by Date() < expires (:317-318). refreshSavedState and toggleSaved treat any non-200 as a failure (:368-380, :414-420): saved-state is retried 3 times with the same token (retrySavedState) and then left nil (heart stays dim), toggles roll back silently. No 401 branch exists (only 403). With a corrected clock the bad token is used for as long as the skew, so the lock-card heart is dead for hours; Settings still says connected.

scenario: First launch on a Mac whose clock is ahead of real time (new VM, dead clock battery, wrong date before NTP), later corrected; user takes screenshots and recordings with Screenshot.app.
expected: Captures made after install are offered on the Shelf whatever the clock was at first launch.
actual_by_code: NotchStores.start stamps recordings.since = Date() once and never moves it (NotchStores.swift:88-89). RecordingPickup.collect inserts each filename into the persisted seen set before testing the date (RecordingPickup.swift:79) and drops anything with mtime <= since (:82). With since in the future every capture until real time catches up is rejected AND recorded as seen, so it is never offered even after the clock is fixed (seen persisted by ShelfStore.importNewRecordings).
existing_test: RecordingPickupTests.testOldRecordingIsNeverOfferedYetNeverReconsidered (the 'never reconsidered' half is the defect here)

scenario: A Russian-authored .lrc with comma decimals ('[01:23,45]'), or timestamps written 'mm:ss:xx', is imported or sits in a watched folder.
expected: Parsed, or rejected with a stated reason; a region whose decimal separator is a comma should not make a whole lyric file unusable.
actual_by_code: parseTimestamp (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:200) splits on the first ':' and needs Double(parts[1]); '23,45' and '23:45' both fail, then parseTimedLine throws invalidTimestamp because the raw stamp contains ':' (:143-146). One such line rejects the entire file (malformed issue). The scripted player position path accepts comma decimals (PlayerBridge.swift:98) but the LRC parser does not.

scenario: Lyric files saved in Windows-1251 (common for Russian LRC), UTF-16 or GBK, placed in a watched folder or imported.
expected: Decoded, or a clear 'unsupported encoding' message.
actual_by_code: Every read is String(contentsOf:, encoding: .utf8) (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:164 import, :269 folder scan; also :409, :492). A non-UTF-8 file throws a non-LocalLyricsDocument error, which the scan files as issue .unreadable (:272-275) with no encoding fallback or detection. The owner's locales (ru/uz) are the ones where cp1251 files are likely.

scenario: A UTF-8 LRC saved by Windows Notepad with a BOM whose first line is '[ti:Title]' or '[00:12.00]First line'.
expected: BOM ignored; tags read; first line kept.
actual_by_code: The parser never strips U+FEFF: raw.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:56) then metadataTag requires line.hasPrefix("[ti:") (:193-197) and parseTimedLine requires remainder.first == "[" (:140). If Foundation keeps the BOM when decoding with encoding: .utf8 (not verified here), the first tag is lost (so title/artist/length matching in LocalLyricsLibrary.lookup :305-312 can fail) or, with a stamp on line 1, the first lyric line is skipped silently (empty timestamps -> continue, :90).

scenario: Mac with a Turkish (or Azerbaijani) region/language; the player says 'I Want It All' or 'KISS', the LRC tag says 'i want it all' or 'Kiss'.
expected: Titles compare equal, case-insensitively, so the local file auto-matches.
actual_by_code: LocalLyricsLibrary.normalized folds with locale: .current (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:605-607). A CoreFoundation probe on this Mac (CFStringFold, case-insensitive + diacritic-insensitive, the call behind NSString folding) gives en_US: 'kiss'/'kiss'; tr_TR: 'KISS' -> 'kıss' but 'Kiss' -> 'kiss', 'I Want' -> 'ı want' but 'i want' -> 'i want'. So under tr_TR an uppercase-I title never equals its lowercase-i twin and lookup() (:316-322) falls to noMatch. LyricsStore.swift:208 and OnlineLyrics.swift:268 already pass locale: nil; LyricsStore.swift:286 shares the .current mistake.
existing_test: LocalLyricsLibraryTests (runs only under the test machine's locale)

scenario: Watched lyrics folder laid out like a music library (Artist/Album/track.lrc), or an existing .lrc is edited in place by an editor or sync client.
expected: New or changed files appear within about 150 ms, as the Settings text and inventory claim ('every .lrc under it ... rescanned within 150 ms of a file event').
actual_by_code: The scan is recursive (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:261-268) but installFolderWatchers opens one O_EVTONLY descriptor per selected folder with [.write,.rename,.delete] (:572-587). That fires only for entries added, removed or renamed directly in that directory. A new file in a subfolder, or a truncate-and-write of an existing .lrc, raises no event; it is seen only at relaunch or Rescan Local Lyrics.

scenario: The local-lyrics index.json cannot be decoded: written by a newer build with an extra enum case (for example a new FileIssue) and then read by an older build, or damaged; builds from several worktrees share one Application Support directory on the owner's Mac.
expected: The old index is kept or moved aside and the user is told; bindings and folder bookmarks survive.
actual_by_code: loadState returns an empty State() on any decode failure (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:624-630). Init then rescans (:159) and persist() overwrites index.json (:614-618) with no backup. Added keys are tolerated (decodeIfPresent, :104-116) but an unknown enum raw value in issues or documents throws and wipes every folder, binding and imported-document record at the next write.

scenario: ~/Pictures/Isla is deleted or its volume unmounts while the app runs, or the disk is full, with Save Clipboard Screenshots on; user copies a screenshot.
expected: The folder is recreated or the failure is surfaced; the copy is not lost.
actual_by_code: ScreenshotVault resolves its folder once at init (ScreenshotVault.swift:21-23, resolveFolder) and write() only calls data.write(.atomic) (:115-128), never createDirectory. On failure it logs and completes nil; NotchStores' onImage ignores nil (NotchStores.swift:111, guard let url) and ClipboardStore already consumed the change count, so no text fallback runs either. After the folder vanishes every later image copy silently does nothing until relaunch.

scenario: Watched lyrics folder lives in iCloud Drive with Optimize Mac Storage; most .lrc files are evicted (dataless) on macOS 15 or later.
expected: Launch and the panel stay responsive; evicted files are indexed lazily or skipped without blocking.
actual_by_code: LocalLyricsLibrary.init calls rescanFolders() synchronously on the main actor (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:159) and reads every .lrc with String(contentsOf:) (:269). On macOS 15+ evicted files keep their real names, so the enumerator lists them and each read would materialise the file from iCloud on the main thread, serially, before the first panel exists. F-043 notes the main-thread scan but not dataless downloads or the network dependency. The pre-Sonoma '.name.lrc.icloud' placeholder form would instead be skipped as hidden.

scenario: Signed build, first Spotify token read happens while the keychain answers 'interaction not allowed' (Mac locked when the lock-card heart first asks, or a Login Item launches before the keychain is available).
expected: A transient read failure is retried later; only a dismissed prompt means 'stop asking'.
actual_by_code: CredentialStore.readTokens treats 'no access and no refresh token came back' as refusal and sets refused = true for the life of the process (SpotifyAccount.swift:545-556); every later read returns (nil,nil,nil) (:546-548), so freshAccessToken is nil, tokenUnavailable true and the heart hidden until relaunch or reconnect. Items are written kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly (TokenStore.swift:138). Whether macOS fails such a read on a locked screen is not verified.

scenario: Screen saver starts (no password required) with a track playing and the panel pinned open (hot key open on Music or Lyrics).
expected: Panel folds and the 10 Hz ticker plus 1 Hz Apple event poll stop, as at display sleep, or at least are not left running under the saver.
actual_by_code: No observer for com.apple.screensaver.didstart or any screen-saver signal exists (grep 'screensaver' over Sources is empty). Only screensDidSleep (NotchController.swift:75-98) and the lock notifications stop work. A saver without a password produces neither, so a pinned panel stays open and media.setActive(true) keeps the ticker (MediaController.swift:2070) and the precision poll running until the display finally sleeps. Music keeps the Mac awake, so the saver can run long.

scenario: App Nap on an idle Isla (LSUIElement, panel on screen but fully click-through) while the pointer sampler, boundary timer and clipboard poll depend on prompt timers.
expected: Hover-to-open, lyric line changes and clipboard capture stay on time; or the app opts out of timer coalescing while it has live work.
actual_by_code: No beginActivity, NSProcessInfo activity or NSAppSleepDisabled anywhere (grep empty); bundle.sh sets only NSSupportsAutomaticTermination/SuddenTermination false (Scripts/bundle.sh:83-84). PointerWatcher (8 Hz, tolerance interval/2, PointerWatcher.swift:109-120), ClipboardStore (0.5 s, tolerance 0.2) and the lyric boundary timer are plain Timers. If macOS classifies the window as occluded, timers can be stretched well past those beats; whether it does for a transparent top-of-screen panel is not established.

scenario: Power adapter on a flaky USB-C hub or dock that drops and restores PD every few seconds.
expected: One charger moment per plug-in as the headphones moment does (30 s quiet window), not a bolt every few seconds.
actual_by_code: powerChanged fires onEvent for every false->true external-power transition (AmbientWatch.swift:94-102, pluggedIn :107-110) with no quiet period; only headphones carry repeatQuiet (:163, 30 s). presentAmbient re-arms a fresh 2.2 s moment each time (NotchController.swift:~1345-1368), so each flap re-grows the pill and plays the blur-replace animation.

scenario: Notch MacBook, music playing, frontmost app has long menu titles (Xcode, Photoshop) ending within about 52 pt of the notch's left edge, or crowded right-side status items.
expected: The last menu title and the first status items stay clickable, or the wing yields.
actual_by_code: While a track plays the pill is notch + 104 pt (NotchMetrics.swift:33), about 52 pt each side, and every drawn point answers clicks by design (compactGestureRect, NotchGeometry.swift:~280; inventory 'click target follows the drawn island'). A click on a menu title under the wing opens Isla instead. The synthetic-notch comment records the same trade being decided for unnotched displays; for physical notches no measurement of overlap with real menu layouts is recorded.

scenario: Clock is wrong (ahead) at a launch: Isla starts and prunes the drop inbox.
expected: Only folders genuinely older than 7 days leave; a wrong clock cannot trash cards the Shelf still shows.
actual_by_code: pruneDropInbox computes cutoff = Date() - 7 days from the wall clock (AppPaths.swift:67) and trashes any Dropped/<uuid> whose mtime is older, with no check against live Shelf URLs (:69-71; call at NotchStores.swift:96). A clock a week or more ahead at launch trashes every promised drop, including ones from today, on top of F-019's plain 7-day case. Files go to the Trash, so it is recoverable but unannounced.

scenario: LRCLIB answers 'no lyrics' while the clock is ahead; the clock is then corrected.
expected: The 14-day negative cache expires 14 real days later.
actual_by_code: Misses carry checkedAt = Date() (OnlineLyrics.swift:~344) and are believed while Date().timeIntervalSince(checkedAt) < missLifetime (:335, :367-370). A future checkedAt gives a negative interval, so the miss is believed for 14 days plus the skew (months if the clock was a year off). trim() sorts by checkedAt (:~380), so future-dated entries also count as 'newest' and are the last evicted. The cache is persisted JSON, so it survives relaunch.

scenario: Lid closed, or Mac locked, within 2.2 s of a track change, so a track peek is in flight.
expected: Nothing stale is on the pill after wake or unlock.
actual_by_code: The sleep handler (NotchController.swift:75-98) calls clearAmbient() but not peekWork?.cancel() / isPeeking = false; screenLocked() likewise clears only ambient. peekWork is cancelled only in toggleLyrics, translate, rebuild, sneakPeek and presentAmbient (:526, :555, :775, :1300, :1354). DispatchQueue.asyncAfter counts mach time, which does not advance in sleep, so the remainder of the 2.2 s fires after wake: the pill wakes still widened over the old title for up to 2.2 s. The charger moment got this fix; the peek did not.

scenario: Laptop crosses time zones or DST begins while Isla has been running for days (Login Item, auto time zone on); user then saves a clipboard screenshot.
expected: The 'Screenshot yyyy-MM-dd at HH.mm.ss' name shows the current local time.
actual_by_code: The stamp DateFormatter is a static let with timeZone = .current assigned once (ScreenshotVault.swift:71-77). TimeZone.current is a snapshot, so the name keeps the zone at first use until relaunch (autoupdatingCurrent would follow). Order and the 200-file trim use mtime (:~150-160), so only the names are wrong. Also, a long-lived ShelfStore.ageFormatter is built once (ShelfStore.swift:38-44), but it formats relative text and is unaffected.

scenario: Automatic update check is on; Isla launches as a Login Item before Wi-Fi has joined, and the Mac sleeps each night.
expected: A failed check is retried soon, and 'daily' means roughly once a day.
actual_by_code: startAutomaticIfEnabled schedules one check 20 s after launch and a repeating Timer of 24 h (UpdateCheck.swift:125-141). A failed first check sets .failed and waits for the next 24 h tick. Timer time does not advance during sleep, so a laptop awake about 6 h a day checks about every 4 days; a no-network launch can leave the check failed for days.

scenario: Wall clock steps backward (NTP correction, manual change, VM resume) by a minute or more while a play/pause is in flight, a track change is awaited, or the pointer is mid-dwell.
expected: Short windows still end; nothing stays held for the length of the step.
actual_by_code: Several windows use Date(): PlaybackIntent confirmation (PlaybackIntent.swift:60, >= 1.5 s), awaitingTrackChange grace (MediaController.swift:921, 1.2 s), foreign-session hold (:1384, 10 s), restartExpectedUntil (:937), AmbientWatch repeatQuiet (AmbientWatch.swift:163) and PointerWatcher dwell/grace/rest (PointerWatcher.swift:136-138, 164-194, 254-292). A negative elapsed stays below each threshold, so a command that never confirmed keeps coalescing taps, readings stay held and a close dwell never completes until the clock passes the old stamp. Only the anchor, helper heartbeat and silence watchdog were moved to systemUptime.

scenario: An NTP step of a few seconds lands during playback, between the player's timestamp and Isla's read.
expected: The bar and lyric do not jump by the step.
actual_by_code: reportedPosition adds Date().timeIntervalSince(takenAt) * rate (MediaController.swift:1887-1893) with takenAt from the player's wall clock, so a +5 s step makes one reading 5 s ahead; adopt() takes forward deltas over 0.05 s (forwardTolerance) and then holds the corrective rewind for one extra reading (corroboratesRewind). The ticker itself is safe (monotonicNow, :124, tested). Result: one visible jump of about the step for roughly two polls.

scenario: ProcessInfo.thermalState reaches serious or critical, or Low Power Mode is on, while the lyrics stage or lock card (60/44 pt blurred cover, 10 Hz ticker, karaoke sweep) is on screen.
expected: Isla sheds optional work (blur, ticker rate) or at least does not add heat.
actual_by_code: No thermalState, isLowPowerModeEnabled or power-state observer exists (grep empty). MediaController.positionTickInterval is a fixed 0.1 s (MediaController.swift:330), the blur radii are constants, and SystemAppearance observes only the three accessibility flags. The existing Low Power Mode ledger row covers idle wake-ups only.

scenario: System memory pressure on a 8 GB Mac with a long uptime: artwork decoded at full size (about 36 MB for a 3000 px cover), up to 1000 cached lyric timelines, 40 clipboard entries of up to 256 KiB, 60 Shelf thumbnails.
expected: Caches shrink under pressure.
actual_by_code: No DispatchSource memory-pressure source, NSCache or purge hook exists (grep empty); the online cache is a dictionary trimmed only by count (OnlineLyrics.swift:~375) and artwork is held for the life of the track. Behaviour under pressure is whatever the VM compressor does.

scenario: Isla is driven over Screen Sharing/VNC while the physical display is asleep or blanked (curtain mode, headless Mac mini with a virtual display).
expected: The island and hot keys work for the remote user.
actual_by_code: If the system posts screensDidSleep for the dark physical display, the handler closes the panel, stops the pointer sampler, clipboard poll, ticker and watchdog (NotchController.swift:75-98) until screensDidWake. Panel interactivity is set only by the sampler (onInteractiveChange, :985-987), so a remote session would see no hover or click handling in that stretch. Whether the sleep notification is posted in those modes is not shown by the code.

scenario: User opens Isla.app straight from the mounted DMG or from Downloads (App Translocation) and turns on Launch at Login.
expected: A clear message that the app must be in Applications, or a stable registration.
actual_by_code: launchAtLoginBinding calls SMAppService.mainApp.register() and only logs a failure (SettingsPane.swift:~632-646); there is no check of the bundle's location. From a translocated or read-only volume the registered path may not exist at next login, and ejecting the DMG under a running app is not handled. F-027 covers the silent snap-back, not this install state.

scenario: Lock card or lock pill after a WindowServer connection change (fast user switch, loginwindow restart).
expected: The above-shield space is created on a live connection.
actual_by_code: SkyLight.shared captures SLSMainConnectionID once in a static initialiser (LockScreenPresence.swift:180) and every Calls closure closes over it. A later connection reset would make create/add calls fail silently (create returning 0 is checked, :200-205, but add/remove results are not), leaving the pill under the shield with no log.

scenario: Copy text on an iPhone (Universal Clipboard) with the phone leaving range or asleep, while Clipboard History is on.
expected: The 0.5 s poll never stalls the UI.
actual_by_code: pollNow runs on the main actor (ClipboardStore.swift:174) and reads pasteboard.string(forType:) synchronously (:215). For a Continuity promise the data is fetched at read time. The image path has a bounded retry (12 x 0.5 s, :~290-300) and text has none, so a slow or failing transfer could block the main thread (pointer sampler, animations) for as long as the system waits. Not measured.

scenario: Charger plugged in, or a Bluetooth device appears, while the Mac is asleep; display wakes.
expected: No stale moment on wake for something that happened hours ago.
actual_by_code: ambientAllowed refuses while screensAreAsleep (NotchController.swift:~1380-1386), and powerChanged updates lastPower even when refused (AmbientWatch.swift:94-97) so a plug-in during sleep is swallowed if the IOPS callback precedes screensDidWake. If the callback is delivered after the flag clears (or on a DarkWake), the user gets a 'Charging' moment at wake. The order macOS delivers them in is not visible in code.

scenario: External lyrics volume (USB or SMB) is unmounted and mounted again while Isla runs.
expected: The folder is re-indexed and watched again on mount.
actual_by_code: No NSWorkspace didMount/didUnmount observer exists. Unmount makes rescanFolders keep the old documents and mark the folder unreadable (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:~236-246); the O_EVTONLY descriptor (:572-587) goes stale and is only reinstalled by addFolder or a relaunch. After remount lookups still work from memory, Settings keeps showing the unreadable issue, and new files on the volume are not noticed until Rescan Local Lyrics.

scenario: A file with a modification date in the future (clock-skewed camera, copy from a machine with a wrong clock) is dropped on the Shelf or picked up as a capture.
expected: The card sits in its real place and reads sensibly.
actual_by_code: Cards sort newest-first by date (ShelfStore.swift:274-282); RecordingPickup takes contentModificationDate as the capture date (RecordingPickup.swift:80-83). A future date sorts to the top for as long as it stays future, and age(of:) falls through to 'Just now' while now - date < 60 s, including negative values (ShelfStore.swift:29-31). Minor, but it also makes the card immune to the 60-card trim until the clock catches up.

scenario: Mac set to a Russian region with the system language English (or the reverse); user hovers a Shelf card.
expected: The tooltip date follows the same language as the rest of the card.
actual_by_code: The age label uses RelativeDateTimeFormatter with Locale(identifier: appLanguage) (ShelfStore.swift:38-44) to avoid mixing, but the tooltip is date.formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .shortened) (ShelfPane.swift:161), which uses the system locale and its 12/24 h setting. Month names and clock style can come out in a different language from the label above them.

scenario: Non-US keyboard hardware or layout (ISO, JIS, Dvorak, Colemak) with the default hot keys.
expected: The key named in Settings and the welcome is the key the user presses.
actual_by_code: Bindings are physical key codes with US names (HotKeys.swift:~80-100); keyName returns '#<code>' for any code outside the ANSI table (:98), so ISO section or JIS keys show as '#10'. On Dvorak the default ⌃⌥⌘I fires on the key printed 'G'. The choice is documented as deliberate for Cyrillic users, but the label gives no hint.

scenario: Decimal-comma region (ru_RU, de_DE) with Apple Music or Spotify driven through the AppleScript fallback.
expected: Fractional positions parse the same as in an English region.
actual_by_code: precisePosition reads 'player position as text' and replaces ',' with '.' before parsing (PlayerBridge.swift:98); state replies use integer milliseconds joined with character id 1 (PlayerBridge.swift:~267-300) and are parsed with Double(parts[n]) / 1000 (interpret, :~400-411); seek text is built with String(format:) in the POSIX locale (:180). So the three number paths are locale-safe. Digits in non-ASCII numeral systems (ar-SA) are not exercised.
existing_test: PlayerScriptTests (compile only; no comma parse test)

scenario: Wall clock jumps (NTP step, manual change) while a track plays and the lyric stage is open.
expected: The ticker and lyric timers do not move by the step.
actual_by_code: Anchor extrapolation uses ProcessInfo.systemUptime (MediaController.swift:124, tick() :2083), the boundary timer is armed from the same position, the helper's heartbeat de-duplication and the app's silence watchdog both count systemUptime (helper.m:98-104, NowPlayingFeed.swift:117, 197, 217). The remaining wall-clock uses are listed in the separate wall-clock rows.

scenario: Two clipboard screenshots in the same second, or the DST fall-back hour repeating HH.mm.ss, with Save Clipboard Screenshots on.
expected: Neither file overwrites the other; names stay stable across languages and calendars.
actual_by_code: The stamp pattern uses en_US_POSIX (Gregorian, 24 h) (ScreenshotVault.swift:71-77) and write() appends ' (2)', ' (3)' while fileExists (:115-125), so repeats and the repeated DST hour cannot collide. The trim sorts by mtime, not by name. The only gap is the cached time zone (separate row).

scenario: Mac with no battery (Mac mini, Studio, iMac) opens Settings; Show Charging row.
expected: A switch that can never do anything is not offered.
actual_by_code: AmbientWatch.hasBattery is a static let from readPower() != nil (AmbientWatch.swift:90) and SettingsPane shows the Show Charging row only if it is true (SettingsPane.swift:152). On such Macs readPower is nil so powerChanged (guard let now) never emits.

scenario: Russian UI: Shelf selection count for 1, 2, 5 and 21 cards.
expected: Grammatical in every plural class.
actual_by_code: ru.lproj maps '%d selected' to 'Выбрано %d' (Resources/ru.lproj/Localizable.strings:28), a count-after-label form that needs no inflection; the age text comes from RelativeDateTimeFormatter in ru (ShelfStore.swift:38-44) which handles plurals itself.

scenario: The Now Playing route stays 'healthy' but permanently empty: a macOS update stops trusting perl (mediaremoted answers an empty dictionary, the 15.4 failure) or renames the kMRMediaRemoteNowPlayingInfo* keys while the function symbols still resolve. Spotify or Music plays.
expected: Detect 'helper alive, but never one non-empty record while a scriptable player is running', fall back to the AppleScript route and tell the user why in Settings.
actual_by_code: helper.m:244-262 emits title "" for every missing key, so the record is valid; NowPlayingFeed.swift:457-459 records it as success; MediaController.swift:1072-1074 turns an empty record into .accept, then apply -> clear() (1363, 1700). The only fallback triggers are helper death, 12 s silence (NowPlayingFeed.swift:215-232), 3 failures, or an {error} line (decoder 16). feedDelivered (MediaController.swift:1819-1829) even treats the first EMPTY snapshot of a retry as proof the helper works and drops the fallback. Island says 'Nothing is playing' for ever; no Settings note.
existing_test: NowPlayingRouteTests.testAWakeTriesAgainAndTheFallbackStaysUntilTheHelperSpeaks (counts any snapshot as proof); no test feeds only empty snapshots

scenario: A user's own .lrc carries a standard non-time tag such as [by:someone], [re:LRC Maker], [tool:..], [id:..] or [la:..] (very common in downloaded LRC files). Local library scan or Import LRC.
expected: Unknown [xx:value] header tags are ignored (only [mm:ss.xx] is a time stamp); the file loads.
actual_by_code: LocalLyricsDocument.swift:60-87 recognises only ti, ar, al, ve, length, offset. Any other tag falls to parseTimedLine (136-149): parseTimestamp('by:someone') is nil, and because the text contains ':' it throws invalidTimestamp (144), which aborts the whole parse. The file becomes a .malformed issue in a watched folder (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:276-277) or an swallowed import error. The same parser rejects an LRCLIB payload containing such a tag (OnlineLyrics.swift:99,227 use try?). The 240-track lab corpus has no such tags (REPORT L1), so it never exercised this.

scenario: Import LRC / Add Lyrics Folder / Rescan fail: the picked file is invalid, not UTF-8 (UTF-16 or GBK LRC), unreadable, or the import cannot be written (disk full, read-only support dir).
expected: One section-level message saying why (invalid format, encoding, cannot save); nothing silently dropped.
actual_by_code: NotchViewModel.swift:403 `try? lyricsCoordinator.importLocalFile(at:)`, :412 `try? addFolder`, :420 `try? rescanFolders` discard every error. importLocalFile also silently returns when currentIdentity is nil (LyricsCoordinator.swift:195). Non-UTF-8 files throw a Cocoa error and are filed as .unreadable (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:278-279) with no encoding fallback. User picks a file, the panel closes, nothing happens.

scenario: A track's bound LRC disappears (Application Support deleted or restored without imports/, an imported copy cleared by hand, or a watched-folder file the user bound is deleted). The track plays again, including after a relaunch.
expected: Lookup falls through to folder match/online, or the page offers Remove Local Binding for that track.
actual_by_code: Bindings are persisted but documents are reloaded only if the file exists (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:489-499; rescan drops missing folder docs 284-286) and bindings are never pruned. lookup() returns .invalid(.unreadable) for a binding with no record (301-304). The online fallback needs localLookup == .noMatch (LyricsCoordinator.swift:292), so LRCLIB is never asked. Caption reads 'No lyrics for this track.' (LyricsPresentation.swift:34). The Remove Local Binding button shows only when lyrics.hasLocalOverride (LyricsStage.swift:511), which is set only by import/select in this session and reset on every track change (LyricsCoordinator.swift:266) and never recomputed from the persisted binding. The only escape is Settings 'Clear bindings and timing corrections', which wipes every binding.

scenario: User adds a huge tree as lyrics folder (home directory, an external drive root, a network share with millions of files). Isla then relaunches at login.
expected: Bounded, off-main, cancellable scan with a file-count/depth cap and a visible 'scanning' or 'too large' state; launch never waits on it.
actual_by_code: LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:159 init calls try? rescanFolders() on the main actor; :254-282 enumerates every file with a resource-value stat per entry and reads+parses every .lrc, no cap, no cancellation. NotchStores.init builds the library at controller init, before the panel exists. Result: addFolder hangs the UI during the click, and every later launch (login item included) hangs the main thread for the length of the walk, so the island never appears; fixing it needs hand-editing lyrics-local/index.json. F-043 covers a big lyrics library, not a pathological folder or the launch consequence.

scenario: A corrupt or hand-edited hotkey default: `defaults write com.ctimothe.isla hotkey.openPanel -dict keyCode 99999999999 modifiers 0` (or modifiers over 4294967295).
expected: Out-of-range values are treated as 'cleared'/default and the app launches.
actual_by_code: HotKeys.swift:146-152 casts to [String:Int], checks only >= 0, then calls UInt32(keyCode)/UInt32(modifiers), which traps on overflow. HotKeyCenter.shared is first touched in AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching (AppDelegate.swift:47) via init (HotKeys.swift:233-237). Every launch crashes before the panel is usable; nothing relaunches or enters a safe mode.

scenario: A player reports a non-finite or non-JSON-safe number, e.g. duration/elapsed/rate = inf or NaN for a live HLS stream in a browser tab.
expected: Helper sanitises or drops the value; the route survives.
actual_by_code: helper.m:260-262 copies the raw NSNumber into the payload; emitPayload (91) calls [NSJSONSerialization dataWithJSONObject:options:error:NULL] and then checks `if (!json) return`. For NaN/inf the API raises NSInvalidArgumentException (it does not return nil), on sQueue, uncaught (no @try anywhere in the file), so perl aborts. It reproduces on every restart while the stream plays, so after 3 consecutive failures (NowPlayingFailurePolicy.swift:44) the whole Now Playing route falls back to Music/Spotify only with the generic 'kept stopping' text.
existing_test: none; NowPlayingLifecycleTests cover only the restart policy

scenario: A macOS update removes or renames the private selectors the helper calls (MRMediaRemoteServiceClient sharedServiceClient / activePlayerPath) or changes the signature of MRMediaRemoteSendCommandToPlayer / GetSupportedCommandsForPlayer.
expected: Missing selectors are detected (respondsToSelector), the helper reports routeClosed, and the app says so.
actual_by_code: helper.m:356-359 uses performSelector with no respondsToSelector guard: an existing class that lost the selector raises unrecognized-selector inside publishAttempt on the first publish (startFeed 493), killing perl. Function pointers (typedefs 23-29, dlsym 434-439) are checked only for non-nil, never for signature, so a changed argument list crashes or mis-sends on the first command. Both end as the generic keptStopping fallback after 3 deaths; the route is never classed .routeClosed and a Try Again repeats the crash.

scenario: Helper emits valid JSON that the decoder rejects because a field changed type (e.g. duration becomes a string, playing becomes 0/1 as a string, timestamp missing) after an OS or helper version skew.
expected: Undecodable-but-alive is detected like silence: restart or fall back, with a reason.
actual_by_code: NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:17-21 returns nil unless playing/duration/elapsed/rate/timestamp have exact types; NowPlayingFeed.handle (441-462) silently returns for nil. consume() refreshes lastLineAt on any byte (428) before decoding, so the 12 s silence watchdog never fires, no failure is recorded, no fallback happens, and the island shows nothing for as long as the helper lives. The same holds for a stream of garbage lines.

scenario: Spotify connect succeeds in the browser but the token write fails: disk full, support directory deleted while running (ad-hoc build, file backing), or keychain write refused.
expected: Connected only if the tokens were stored; otherwise show 'could not save the account'.
actual_by_code: TokenStore.write returns a Backing (89-92) and writeFileValues returns false on failure (150-171, no createDirectory, so a deleted support dir fails every later write), but CredentialStore.storeTokens ignores the result and writes the in-memory cache (SpotifyAccount.swift:553-563); store() then sets isConnected = true (277-279). Settings and the heart show connected; at the next launch the init read finds nothing (136-143) and the account is silently gone. A refresh-token rotation that fails to persist the same way strands the old token.
existing_test: TokenStoreTests (round trip, owner-only), none for a failed write

scenario: Keychain or securityd is not ready, or the data-protection read fails transiently (login-item start right after boot or FileVault unlock, keychain locked), while a Spotify account exists.
expected: A transient read error is retried and does not look like 'no account'.
actual_by_code: TokenStore.keychainRead (124-131) maps every non-success status to nil, same as errSecItemNotFound; SpotifyAccount.init (136-143) sets isConnected = false and, for the ad-hoc case, then probes legacy. CredentialStore.readTokens (537-551) sets refused = true when nothing comes back, and that flag is sticky for the whole process, so freshAccessToken returns nil for ever and the heart stays hidden (tokenUnavailable). Only a manual reconnect clears it.

scenario: The Spotify refresh token is dead (user removed access on spotify.com, or invalid_grant) while the cached access token expires.
expected: One failed refresh marks the account 'needs reconnect' in Settings and stops calling Spotify for each track.
actual_by_code: tokenRequest returns nil for any non-200 (SpotifyAccount.swift:255-257); freshAccessToken (302-331) returns nil but never clears the stored tokens or isConnected. Each track change reaches refreshSavedState (339-350) and trackMetadata (456-464), so each one POSTs a failing refresh to accounts.spotify.com. Only tokenUnavailable is set, which hides the heart (LockScreenCard.swift:836) but is not read by SettingsPane (489-492 shows only apiBlocked), so Settings still reads connected.

scenario: Isla is quit, crashes or is relaunched (update, login) between pressing Connect Spotify and the browser returning to isla://spotify-callback.
expected: The callback completes the sign-in or tells the user to start again.
actual_by_code: verifier and authorizationState live only in memory (SpotifyAccount.swift:88-94,170-178). The scheme relaunches the app, handleCallback (193-210) finds verifier nil and returns without any message. The user sees Spotify's success page and Isla still offers Connect.
existing_test: SpotifyAccountTests covers state mismatch, not a missing verifier

scenario: Authorization ends without an account: user clicks Cancel on Spotify's consent page (error=access_denied), or the token exchange fails (offline, 5xx, 429, expires_in not an Int).
expected: A one-line result in Settings (denied / could not connect, try again).
actual_by_code: handleCallback needs `code` (SpotifyAccount.swift:194-197) and returns silently without it; for a code, the single-use verifier and state are consumed before the request (205-206); exchange -> tokenRequest nil -> return (233) with no state published. The browser page and Isla both show success or nothing; a retry needs a fresh Connect.

scenario: User deletes ~/Pictures/Isla (or empties it with Finder) while Isla runs with Save Clipboard Screenshots on, then copies a screenshot.
expected: The vault recreates its folder and saves the capture.
actual_by_code: ScreenshotVault.resolveFolder runs once at init (19-44); write() (115-137) never creates the directory, so Data.write(.atomic) fails with no-such-file and completion(nil); NotchStores.swift:94-98 returns on nil with no message. Every capture is dropped silently until relaunch, and the change count was already marked seen, so the copy is not retried.

scenario: Disk full or read-only Pictures and Application Support while a copy carries both an image and text (spreadsheet range, rich text) with Save Clipboard Screenshots on.
expected: Tell the user the capture was not saved; record the text instead.
actual_by_code: ClipboardStore.pollNow (198-210) hands the PNG to onImage and returns; deliverImage (324-333) only falls back to text for undecodable or absent images. The vault write failure (ScreenshotVault.swift:127-133 -> completion(nil)) is swallowed at NotchStores.swift:94-98: image lost, text lost, no card, no notice. recordings.seen and shelf defaults writes fail the same silent way.

scenario: The update check receives a tampered release payload (corporate TLS-inspecting proxy, hijacked release) whose html_url is not on github.com/ctimothe/isla-mac, e.g. a phishing https URL or a file:// path to an app.
expected: Only an https URL on github.com under the project's path is ever opened; anything else is .failed.
actual_by_code: UpdateCheck.swift:83-96 decodes html_url as any URL; only tag_name is validated (numeric dotted). SettingsPane.swift:578-581 passes it to NSWorkspace.shared.open under a 'Download Isla x.y' button with the note 'Quit Isla, then replace it'. A file:// URL to an .app launches it. tag_name stays safe (non-numeric tags are never newer).
existing_test: UpdateCheckTests (draft, newer, prerelease; no hostile URL)

scenario: LRCLIB returns a synced lyric that LocalLyricsDocument refuses (a [by:] or [Verse 1: Name] section line, a [length:225] seconds value, an out-of-order stamp, stacked stamps).
expected: Salvage lines the parser understands, or at least do not remember a parse failure as 'LRCLIB has nothing'.
actual_by_code: OnlineLyrics.timeline (97-100) and bestMatch (227) use try? parse, so a throw becomes .none; lookUp finishes with .none; OnlineLyricsCache.remember stores a miss with searched = true (343-344) for missLifetime = 14 days (302). The lyric is then not retried for two weeks unless the user presses Retry, even after the catalogue entry is fixed. Related to F-009 (stacked stamps), but the 14-day caching and the other triggers are new.

scenario: Network down for several minutes (or DNS failing, TLS clock error) with Look Up Lyrics Online on, while a song plays; then the network returns.
expected: The caption says the service could not be reached, and a lookup resumes when the network comes back.
actual_by_code: A transport error returns .failed (OnlineLyrics.swift:134-136); LyricsCoordinator.swift:349-351 maps onlineFailed to .noLocalLyrics, which the caption renders 'No lyrics found.' (LyricsPresentation.swift:30-31): outage and absence read the same. Retries run only at 5, 30 and 120 s (LyricsCoordinator.swift:81,169-179) and then stop for that song; there is no NWPathMonitor or wake hook (grep finds none). A user retry after the three are spent never schedules another because retryAttempt stays at 3.

scenario: LRCLIB answers 429 or 5xx (or is down) during a playlist.
expected: Honour Retry-After, back off globally, stop hammering a community service.
actual_by_code: Any non-2xx except 404 is .failed (OnlineLyrics.swift:90-92,146-150); Retry-After is never read (grep: no 429/Retry-After in Sources). Each track change issues the exact query plus up to two searches (141-155), and each failure schedules three more rounds (LyricsCoordinator.swift:169-179). A skip cancels the previous request but nothing is shared across tracks, so a 20-song playlist during an outage sends about 9 requests per song.

scenario: Spotify's Web API returns 429 (development-mode quota) or 5xx while connected.
expected: Honour Retry-After; skip optional calls (ISRC/duration, which nothing reads) while limited.
actual_by_code: refreshSavedState retries three times at 2, 4, 8 s on any non-200 (SpotifyAccount.swift:357-368,374-382); trackMetadata (456-478) returns nil but is called for every Spotify track (MediaController.swift:631) and does not set apiBlocked on 429, so it keeps firing on each track change and extends the penalty. Retry-After is never read.

scenario: A watched lyrics folder is deleted and recreated at the same path (sync client replacing the directory), or its bookmark is corrupt.
expected: Fall back to the stored path, as the folder watcher and the Shelf do.
actual_by_code: rescanFolders does `let url = try? resolve(folder)` and treats nil as unreachable (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:238-243); resolve throws when the bookmark's target is gone or the data is bad (558-570). The path fallback exists only for no-bookmark or stale cases and in installFolderWatchers (576), so the watcher is attached to the path while rescans keep reporting .unreadable for a folder that is present and full of lyrics; the user must remove and re-add it.

scenario: Lyrics folder lives in iCloud Drive/Dropbox with Optimize Storage or on a flaky SMB share, so .lrc files are dataless or the mount stalls during a scan.
expected: Scans never block the UI and never force downloads.
actual_by_code: rescanFolders (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:261-281) reads each file with String(contentsOf:) on the main actor, at init (159), on addFolder, and 150 ms after every folder event (589-595). Reading a dataless file triggers a synchronous materialisation (network) on the main thread; a half-dead mount stalls it until the filesystem times out. The sync-client event storm re-runs it. F-043 notes main-thread parsing, not blocking I/O.

scenario: The main thread stalls for more than 12 s (Shelf open on a hung SMB share per F-022, dataless lyric read, a pasteboard owner that never answers) while the helper is healthy and chatting.
expected: A stall in Isla is not read as helper silence.
actual_by_code: Lines are timestamped only when consume runs on the main actor (NowPlayingFeed.swift:422-432), but the silence check also runs on main (215-232) against the uptime clock, which does not stop during a stall. When the loop recovers, the repeating Timer can run before the queued consume hops; lastLineAt is then more than 12 s old, so a healthy helper is killed and a failure charged. The sleep fix (systemUptime) does not cover stalls; repeated stalls consume the 8-per-5-minutes budget.

scenario: Automation consent for Music/Spotify is denied (or revoked in Privacy settings) and the Now Playing route is closed, so the AppleScript fallback is the only route.
expected: Settings names the missing permission and offers a button to Privacy & Security > Automation.
actual_by_code: PlayerBridge.interpret maps -1743 to .unknown (395-400); currentState drops .unknown states (105-121); refreshFromPlayers on nil calls clear() (MediaController.swift:1831-1834). Result: 'Nothing is playing.' with a playing app. No code references -1743 for the user (grep shows only comments); the route-failure note says only 'Music and Spotify can be seen'. On the helper route the same denial silently hides shuffle/repeat, the Spotify heart, and precision sync.

scenario: macOS changes the SkyLight SPI signatures (symbols still exported) before a lock.
expected: A version/ABI gate or breaker so a lock cannot take the app down; the pill is merely hidden over the shield.
actual_by_code: SkyLight.init? (LockScreenPresence.swift:159-190) only checks that dlsym finds the eight symbols, then unsafeBitCasts them to fixed @convention(c) types. A changed argument list would crash inside lift() on the first lock (screenLocked -> lockPresence.apply, NotchController.swift:249) with no OS-version check and no 'disable SPI after a crash' memory. Isla then stays dead (see the crash scenario).

scenario: /usr/bin/perl is replaced by an xcode-select style shim, or is no longer arm64e-compatible with the helper dylib, after a macOS update.
expected: A single clear failure state; no repeated system dialogs.
actual_by_code: launch() only checks isExecutableFile(/usr/bin/perl) (NowPlayingFeed.swift:263). If the binary is a shim that raises a developer-tools install prompt, each restart (up to 3), each wake retry (MediaController.swift:1809-1815 blocks only readerRefused) and each Try Again can raise it again. A dlopen refusal exits 3 and reads 'macOS blocked Isla's reader' (a quarantine message) although the cause differs; stderr is /dev/null (276) so the reason is lost.

scenario: Transport command (play/pause/next/shuffle/repeat) is issued in the instant Music or Spotify quits, or while the AppleScript queue is backed up behind a hung script.
expected: A quit player is never relaunched by Isla.
actual_by_code: PlayerBridge.send checks app.isRunning on the caller's thread (199-200) and then queues Script.command, which has no `if it is running` guard (358-364; same for playbackModes 330-349). Apple events to `tell application id` relaunch a quit app; the window is as wide as the queue backlog (a hung script holds the serial queue for the Apple event timeout, F-025). F-041 lists only the artwork script.

scenario: Held or fallback route, Spotify beachballs, and the user taps Next/Previous several times.
expected: Stale taps expire; at most one is executed when the player recovers.
actual_by_code: Each tap is a separate runScript(.transport) on the serial utility queue (PlayerBridge.swift:480-500) with no timeout or expiry; MediaController.next()/previous() (870-887) do not coalesce. When the hung event times out (up to ~2 min) all queued skips run back-to-back. Play/pause is coalesced by PlaybackIntent; skips are not.

scenario: A song is held under a film while Spotify is hung and answers nothing to the state query.
expected: Keep the last known state without lying.
actual_by_code: heldPlayerState returns .unknown after the Apple event times out; syncHeldPlayer keeps the song as last known (MediaController.swift:1332-1338), so no false 'Nothing is playing'. The reply can take up to the default Apple event timeout, during which play/pause state may be stale.

scenario: Fallback or held route: the Spotify artwork request fails (offline, DNS, captive portal HTML) at the moment a track starts.
expected: The cover is asked for again when the network returns or after a delay.
actual_by_code: refreshFromPlayers sets artworkKey = state.key before fetching (MediaController.swift:1853-1856); PlayerBridge.artwork returns nil on any error (237-243) with no retry. Because artworkKey now equals the track key, later polls skip the fetch, so the cover stays a placeholder for the whole track. shouldAskForArtwork explicitly refuses on the fallback route (1645-1655).

scenario: A cover under the 4 MB byte cap but with extreme pixel dimensions (decompression bomb or a 12000 px scan).
expected: Decode with a pixel cap or thumbnail API.
actual_by_code: NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:34-37 bounds encoded bytes only; MediaController.decodeArtwork (1677-1696) creates NSBitmapImageRep and cgImage at full size on a utility queue. A highly compressible PNG can allocate gigabytes in-process, and the image then feeds two blurs. F-044 covers a 3000 px cover, not a hostile or huge one.

scenario: Spotify returns 401 for a still-unexpired cached access token (revoked, or the Mac clock was wrong when it was issued).
expected: 401 invalidates the cached token and triggers one refresh.
actual_by_code: freshAccessToken serves the cached token while Date() < expiresAt (SpotifyAccount.swift:309-313). refreshSavedState treats 401 as a generic non-200 and retries three times with the same token (364-367); toggleSaved rolls the heart back (407-409). The heart stays unknown/hollow until the local expiry passes.

scenario: lyrics-local/index.json is corrupt, truncated by disk errors, or written by a newer build with an unknown origin value, then read by this build.
expected: Keep a backup, recover what decodes, and tell the user.
actual_by_code: loadState (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:624-630) returns an empty State on any decode error. The next persist() (614-618) overwrites the file, so selected folders, bindings and unassigned imports are lost with no copy, and the imports/*.lrc files are orphaned. A single bad enum raw value in StoredDocument.origin is enough.

scenario: online lyrics cache.json or offsets.json is corrupt or oversized.
expected: Bad entries are skipped; a large cache does not delay launch.
actual_by_code: OnlineLyricsCache.load (OnlineLyrics.swift:363-373) and LyricsStore.loadLocalTrackOffsets (290-298) decode the whole dictionary as one unit, so one bad entry drops everything; the next save overwrites. The cache loads synchronously on the main actor from NotchStores/LyricsCoordinator init with only an entry-count cap (1,000 full timelines), so a big file decodes on the launch path.

scenario: lyrics.userOffset in defaults is NaN or far outside +-3 s (hand edit, restore from an older build with a wider range), or Set Lyric Delay receives NaN.
expected: The value is clamped on read; NaN is rejected.
actual_by_code: LyricsStore.swift:42-51 clamps only in didSet, and Swift does not run didSet for the property's initial value, so the stored value is used raw until the slider moves. With NaN, `clamped != userOffset` is true, the observer assigns NaN again (no recursion) and returns before persisting; lead/position arithmetic then carries NaN (SetLyricDelayIntent returns it, IslaIntents.swift:164-167). Lines compare false for the rest of the session.

scenario: A defaults key holds the wrong type: shelf.urls as a string, recordings.since as a string, a bookmarks array with different length.
expected: Ignore the bad value, keep working, and rewrite it.
actual_by_code: ShelfStore.storedURLs (143-148) uses stringArray, which returns nil for a wrong type, so the shelf loads empty and the next persist() overwrites the old list. NotchStores.start only stamps recordings.since when the key is missing (72-74) while ShelfStore.importNewRecordings (218) needs an actual Date, so a mistyped value disables screen-capture pickup permanently and silently. Length mismatch of paths and bookmarks is handled (146).

scenario: Shelf persist with an unbookmarkable card on a dead or hanging network mount, then any add/remove.
expected: Bookmark creation never blocks the main thread on unreachable volumes.
actual_by_code: ShelfStore.persist (411-434) calls makeBookmark for every card without a cached bookmark on every change, on the main actor; failures are not cached ('tried again at the next save'). Each retry stats the dead mount, so adding one screenshot can freeze the UI for the mount timeout. F-022 covers refreshFromDisk, not this save path.

scenario: The app that owns the pasteboard hangs or provides data lazily and slowly (Office, remote desktop) when a copy lands.
expected: Isla never blocks reading the pasteboard.
actual_by_code: pollNow (ClipboardStore.swift:174-217) reads readObjects, data(forType:) and string(forType:) synchronously on the main actor every time the change count moves; a lazy provider that never answers blocks until the pasteboard server times out, and the 0.5 s timer then retries on the next change. movieData() and TIFF reads are the same path.

scenario: The on-device translation engine hangs (translation daemon dead, model download stalled) after the user stops typing.
expected: A timeout, then the next engine or a failure with Retry.
actual_by_code: Translator.translate (407-459) awaits run(candidate) with no timeout; the only cap is the token limit for the model (502-504). A hung TranslationSession or LanguageModelSession keeps isTranslating true and 'Translating...' up until the next keystroke cancels the task; the pair is never failed over. The 218 s run is documented in the file header.

scenario: MyMemory answers HTTP 429/403/5xx, or a captive portal answers 200 with HTML.
expected: Quota/limit or 'unreachable' shown according to the cause.
actual_by_code: OnlineTranslation.translate ignores the HTTP status (75) and decodes the body (92-123). HTML or non-JSON becomes .unreachable ('not reachable right now'), which is right for a portal. A 429 or 403 with a JSON body becomes .refused (119-120) -> 'The translation could not be completed.' plus Retry (Translator.swift:454-458), so a rate limit is presented as a transient error and Retry repeats it.

scenario: The system clock is stepped forward or back by tens of seconds mid-track (manual change, VM resume, NTP after wake) while playing a non-scriptable player.
expected: The position clock does not jump.
actual_by_code: reportedPosition (MediaController.swift:1877-1893) ages the helper's elapsed by Date() minus the MediaRemote timestamp (wall clock); a forward step adds the whole step to the position (a negative age is ignored, 1889). The helper re-serves the same timestamp pair, so the jump repeats each report. Precision sync corrects only Spotify and Music; browsers/podcast apps stay wrong until the next real reading. The monotonic clock is used only for the precision loop.

scenario: Isla.app is dragged to the Trash, moved, replaced in place, or the DMG it runs from is ejected while it is running.
expected: Keep working, and say what is missing if a resource disappears.
actual_by_code: The running process survives; the helper keeps its mapped dylib. On the next helper restart Bundle.main.path(forResource:) is nil -> onUnavailable(.cannotStart) (NowPlayingFeed.swift:263-266) -> fallback with 'could not start' (accurate, but it does not say the app was moved). localized() degrades to English keys (Strings.swift:12-19). A replace-in-place gets a new helper/dylib against the old process (see the decoder-skew scenario). SMAppService login item is not re-checked until Settings opens.

scenario: Isla crashes (any cause above) or is killed for memory.
expected: A crash does not leave the user with no island and no way back; repeated launch crashes are detected.
actual_by_code: No crash handler, launch counter, safe mode or KeepAlive exists (grep: nothing). The app has no Dock icon, menu item or window, so after a crash the only signs are a missing island and dead hot keys; relaunch needs Spotlight/Finder or an App Intent. The helper exits on stdin EOF (helper.m:499-511), so no orphan. Combined with the persisted-state crashes above, a bad key means a launch crash at every login.

scenario: The Application Support folder is deleted while Isla runs (cleanup tool, user).
expected: Every store recreates what it needs, or says it cannot.
actual_by_code: Recreate on write: OnlineLyricsCache (OnlineLyrics.swift:405-412), LyricsStore offsets (300-306), LocalLyricsLibrary.persist (614-618), dropInbox (AppPaths.swift:47-58). No recreate: TokenStore.writeFileValues (TokenStore.swift:150-171), so a Spotify reconnect or token refresh cannot persist on an ad-hoc build and fails silently (see the token scenario). In-memory imported lyric records stay until relaunch; after relaunch bound tracks hit the dangling-binding trap above.

scenario: Disk full or home volume read-only: UserDefaults-backed state (shelf.urls, bookmarks, hotkeys, settings) cannot be flushed.
expected: Settings that matter surface an error; at least the app is not silently different after relaunch.
actual_by_code: All settings and shelf lists use UserDefaults.set with no error channel (ShelfStore.swift:411-434, HotKeys.swift:155-168, LyricsStore.swift:49). Nothing in Sources checks for free space or write errors on those paths, so a shelf, shortcut or lyric delay change can look applied and revert at the next launch; file stores (vault, cache, index) log or swallow errors (Log.shelf/storage only).

The hot key reads NSPasteboard.general.string(forType: .string) with no opt-out check (AppDelegate.swift:49-52) and hands it to controller.translate, which shows it in full (cover is off by default) and, for an online-only language, sends it to api.mymemory.translated.net after 320 ms.

scenario: Copy from a manager or tool that flags its secret with a legacy or non-nspasteboard marker (de.petermaurer.TransientPasteboardType, com.agilebits.onepassword, net.antelle.keeweb, com.typeit4me.clipping, 'Pasteboard generator type') or sets no marker at all (Electron-based managers).

The ledger row 'Copy from a manager that sets no opt-out type' only says it is recorded in memory and cover mode hides it.

scenario: Copy a secret while the Mac is locked (Universal Clipboard arrival from a phone, or a remote paste), then unlock. Clipboard History on.
expected: Per the inventory, 'locking stops the clipboard poll, so copies made while locked are not recorded': the copy made during the lock is never recorded.
actual_by_code: suspendForIdleScreen stops the timer (NotchStores.swift:138-139). The resume path calls refreshClipboardPolling() with settingChanged false, which calls start() (NotchStores.swift:146-148). start() deliberately keeps the old lastChangeCount baseline (ClipboardStore.swift:115-118), so the first poll after unlock sees a moved counter and records whatever was copied during the lock. Only startFresh() re-baselines, and resume never uses it.

scenario: The README privacy table and the 'Nothing leaves the Mac unless you turn it on' sentence versus every outbound request Isla can make with no switch on: Spotify cover art, Apple-event/Web-API calls per Spotify track.
expected: Every outbound request (host, payload, trigger) appears in the README and checklist, and anything that leaves the machine defaults off (CLAUDE.md hard constraint).
actual_by_code: PlayerBridge.artwork fetches the Spotify scripting dictionary's https artwork URL with URLSession.shared whenever Spotify is the shown player (PlayerBridge.swift:230-244), with no setting; its own comment calls it 'the one thing the app ever fetches'. README.md:55-66 lists four requests and says nothing leaves otherwise. Full inventory: LRCLIB get+search (OnlineLyrics.swift:46,50, opt-in), MyMemory GET (OnlineTranslation.swift:20, opt-in), accounts.spotify.com authorize/token and api.spotify.com me/tracks, me/tracks/contains, tracks/{id} (SpotifyAccount.swift:179,251,350,397,465, opt-in), api.github.com releases/latest (UpdateCheck.swift:44, opt-in), Spotify CDN cover (no switch).

scenario: Hostile or compromised cover URL: Spotify's scripting dictionary returns an https URL that redirects to a large or slow body on any host.
expected: Cover fetches are limited to the Spotify CDN host family, size-capped, time-capped, and decoded off the main thread.
actual_by_code: Only the scheme is checked (PlayerBridge.swift:237). URLSession.shared.dataTask follows redirects, has no byte cap and default 60 s timeout, and NSImage(data:) decodes whatever arrives (PlayerBridge.swift:240-241) in the unsandboxed process. Helper-path artwork is capped at 4 MB (NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:49), this path is not.
