expected: Only an https URL on github.com under the project's repository is ever opened; anything else is treated as a failed check.
actual_by_code: Release.html_url is decoded as an arbitrary URL (UpdateCheck.swift:84-89) and 'Download Isla x' calls NSWorkspace.shared.open(page) (SettingsPane.swift:580). file:///Applications/..., a custom scheme or an off-domain URL would all be opened on click. No TLS pinning, and the shared session follows redirects (UpdateCheck.swift:50).

scenario: Downgrade, replay and unsigned-download chain of the updater: an old but higher-than-local tag, a re-served older response, or a release asset swapped after publication.
expected: A user is told only about a verifiably newer, integrity-checked release; the download is verifiable.
actual_by_code: isNewer only compares dotted numbers (UpdateCheck.swift:100-115), drafts and prereleases are excluded (:92-93). The user then downloads an ad-hoc DMG by hand; the SHA-256 is published in the same release notes on the same channel (Scripts/release.sh:182-183), so it adds no independence. README.md:17-20 tells users to run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on the bundle, which removes the Gatekeeper check on the app and its nested dylib.

scenario: A local process swaps Contents/Resources/libislamedia.dylib in a user-owned /Applications/Isla.app (install.sh ditto leaves it user-writable) with its own ad-hoc-signed dylib.
expected: Isla verifies the helper's identity (team id, hash or code requirement) before handing its path to a platform binary, so the helper cannot run attacker code under Isla's TCC identity.
actual_by_code: launch() takes Bundle.main.path(forResource:ofType:) (NowPlayingFeed.swift:136-137) and runs /usr/bin/perl -e 'DynaLoader::dl_load_file($ARGV[0])' (NowPlayingFeed.swift:245,269-270). No signature, hash or ownership check; perl has no library validation, so any signed dylib loads and runs as a child of Isla, where Automation and Files and Folders grants attributed to Isla apply. Diagnostics only reports quarantine and signature text (Diagnostics.swift:130-132).
existing_test: none (Scripts/test-gatekeeper.sh checks the shipped bundle, not tamper)

scenario: Isla is launched with PERL5OPT, PERL5LIB, PERL5DB or VERSIONER_PERL_* in its environment (launchctl setenv, a login item environment, a wrapper script).
expected: The perl host runs with a scrubbed environment so only the intended one-liner and dylib execute.
actual_by_code: Process() is configured with executableURL, arguments, pipes only; task.environment is never set (NowPlayingFeed.swift:261-286), so the child inherits Isla's full environment, including variables perl and its macOS versioner shim honour. Whether the macOS 26/27 perl stub still reads them cannot be settled from code.

scenario: A player publishes a Now Playing record whose duration, elapsed or rate is Infinity or NaN (browser live stream, AVPlayer indefinite duration) while Music Only is off or before the source policy runs.
expected: The helper drops or zeroes the non-finite number and keeps running.
actual_by_code: helper.m copies info[@"kMRMediaRemoteNowPlayingInfoDuration"] straight into the payload (helper.m:260-262) and emitPayload calls [NSJSONSerialization dataWithJSONObject:...error:NULL] (helper.m:91). NSJSONSerialization raises NSInvalidArgumentException for NaN/Inf rather than returning nil, so the block on sQueue dies and perl exits, spending the restart budget (3 failures leads to scripting fallback). Not provable from code that macOS ever delivers Infinity.
existing_test: none (NowPlayingPayloadDecoderTests cover the Swift side only)

scenario: Any app (or a web page via the Media Session API when Music Only is off) publishes artwork bytes that are a crafted or decompression-bomb image.
expected: Untrusted image bytes are decoded with bounded dimensions (CGImageSource thumbnail) or out of process.
actual_by_code: Helper artwork passes a 4 MB base64 limit (NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:49-52) and is then decoded in Isla's own process via NSBitmapImageRep at full pixel size (MediaController.swift:1672-1696 per backlog F-044). No pixel-count cap. Whether decode happens before the Music Only policy drops the session was not traced.

scenario: A foreign website or app opens isla://spotify-callback?code=X&state=Y while no sign-in is in flight, or with a wrong state while one is.
expected: Ignored, and a wrong state does not consume or cancel the pending request.
actual_by_code: handleCallback requires verifier and authorizationState (SpotifyAccount.swift:196-202) and returns on mismatch without clearing either, so a forged callback is dropped and the real one still works. Verifier is 64 and state 32 SecRandom bytes (:172-176) and compared in constant time (:213-218). Only the happy path clears them (:205-206).
existing_test: none: grep of Tests finds no handleCallback reference, although the ledger row cites 'callback parsing' in SpotifyAccountTests

scenario: User denies consent in the browser (callback carries error=access_denied and no code), or clicks Connect twice, or abandons the flow.
expected: The pending state and verifier are cleared on an error callback and expire after a few minutes; a second Connect invalidates the first deterministically.
actual_by_code: handleCallback returns on a missing code (SpotifyAccount.swift:194-197) and never reads error, so verifier and authorizationState stay armed for the life of the process; beginAuthorization simply overwrites them (:170-177) so the first browser tab's callback is dropped silently. The host check also accepts any path containing 'spotify-callback' (:194).

scenario: Signed (Developer ID) build: a token write to the data-protection keychain fails (device locked, errSecInteractionNotAllowed, quota), then the lock card refreshes the token.
expected: A failed keychain write is reported and the old keychain value is not preferred over a newer stored one.
actual_by_code: TokenStore.write falls back to the 0600 JSON file when keychainWrite fails and returns .file (TokenStore.swift:90-93); read() prefers the keychain value whenever one exists (:62-65). Spotify rotates refresh tokens (SpotifyAccount.swift:95-99), so the stale keychain refresh token is read next while the fresh one sits in plaintext on disk. CredentialStore.storeTokens ignores the Backing result (SpotifyAccount.swift:553-563). Read also mixes accounts across backings.

scenario: Upgrade from the ad-hoc 0.1/0.2 releases (token file) to a Developer ID build (keychain).
expected: The old plaintext spotify-credentials.json is migrated and deleted so no refresh token stays on disk (and in Time Machine) beside the keychain.
actual_by_code: Nothing removes the file on first successful keychain write. delete() clears it only on Disconnect (TokenStore.swift:96-103). importLegacy copies from the login keychain only (SpotifyAccount.swift:521-530). The file keeps the last ad-hoc-era access and refresh tokens indefinitely.

scenario: Token file creation window and backups: ad-hoc build writes spotify-credentials.json.
expected: The file is created 0600 from the first byte and excluded from backup.
actual_by_code: data.write(.atomic) runs first and setAttributes 0600 afterwards (TokenStore.swift:160-165), so the renamed file briefly has default umask permissions; no isExcludedFromBackup is set, so Time Machine copies refresh tokens. ~/Library is 0700 so exposure is small.

scenario: User revokes Isla at spotify.com/account/apps (or the refresh token otherwise becomes invalid_grant), then keeps playing Spotify.
expected: Isla detects invalid_grant once, clears the account and tells Settings to reconnect, instead of retrying forever.
actual_by_code: tokenRequest returns nil for any non-200 (SpotifyAccount.swift:255-257); freshAccessToken returns nil but never clears tokens (:314-319). isConnected stays true, each track change runs refreshSavedState and trackMetadata, each firing a POST to accounts.spotify.com with the dead refresh token. CredentialStore.refused only latches when both tokens are absent (:545-548).

scenario: Disconnect Spotify, then expect the grant to be gone.
expected: Settings tells the user the grant remains valid server-side until removed at spotify.com/account/apps (Spotify has no token revocation endpoint).
actual_by_code: disconnect() only clears local tokens and cache (SpotifyAccount.swift:282-289); the copy in Settings and README says nothing about server-side revocation.

scenario: The Spotify track id from AppleScript contains characters outside base62 (malformed or hostile 'spotify:track:...' value) and is interpolated into Web API URLs.
expected: The id is validated as 22 base62 characters before any request.
actual_by_code: PlayerBridge.spotifyTrackID only strips the prefix (PlayerBridge.swift:85) and the id is interpolated raw into ids=, /me/tracks?ids= and /v1/tracks/ URLs (SpotifyAccount.swift:350,397,465). An id containing '&', '?' or '/' would inject query parameters or change the path, carrying the Bearer token. Source is Spotify's own app, so exposure is low.

scenario: Translate Online sends text to MyMemory.
expected: Sensitive text is sent in a POST body, never in a URL that proxies, CDNs and server logs retain.
actual_by_code: The text is the q query item of a GET (OnlineTranslation.swift:46-62), so the full sentence (up to 480 chars per request) is in the URL and the request line. The disclosure (Settings note, README) says 'the text', not that it is URL-logged.

scenario: Translate Online with text containing '+' (C++, 2+2, phone numbers +998...).
expected: The service receives the literal plus sign.
actual_by_code: URLComponents.queryItems leaves '+' unescaped (OnlineTranslation.swift:46-62), and the service form-decodes '+' as a space, so '2+2=4' is translated as '2 2=4'. No test passes a plus sign.

scenario: Inspect what the shared URLSession leaves on disk after online translation, lyric lookups and Spotify calls.
expected: Requests carrying private text or tokens use an ephemeral configuration (no URLCache, no cookies), or the README says what is cached.
actual_by_code: Every call uses URLSession.shared (OnlineTranslation.swift:66, OnlineLyrics.swift:119, UpdateCheck.swift:50, SpotifyAccount.swift:125,353,404, PlayerBridge.swift:240), which has the default disk URLCache (~/Library/Caches/<bundle id>/Cache.db) and persistent HTTPCookieStorage. Whether MyMemory/LRCLIB/Spotify responses are cacheable (and so store the translated source text and the played-track queries in the URL key) depends on their headers; not provable from code.

scenario: The OnlineLyrics comment says the lookup sends 'no identifier'. A Cloudflare-fronted API sets a cookie on the first response.
expected: No cookie is stored or replayed, so there is no cross-request identifier.
actual_by_code: URLSession.shared stores and replays cookies (HTTPCookieStorage.shared); no request sets httpShouldHandleCookies = false or uses an ephemeral session (OnlineLyrics.swift:119, OnlineTranslation.swift:66). The claim in OnlineLyrics.swift:20-21 and the README is untested.

scenario: MyMemory (or a MITM) answers with numeric entities that decode to control or bidi scalars (‮, �).
expected: Translated output is sanitised like Now Playing text: bidi overrides and controls stripped before display and before the copy button.
actual_by_code: unescapingEntities turns any valid &#..; into a scalar (OnlineTranslation.swift:193-215); no filtering follows, and the result goes to output and copyOutput (Translator.swift:560-564). The Now Playing decoder strips bidi controls (NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:57-63); translation and lyric paths do not.

scenario: An LRC (watched folder or LRCLIB) contains a section label after a timestamp: '[00:10.00][Verse 1: Drake] text' or '[Intro: Kanye]'.
expected: A bracketed label that is not a timestamp is kept as lyric text.
actual_by_code: parseTimedLine loops while the remainder starts with '['; for rawTimestamp 'Verse 1: Drake', parseTimestamp is nil and, because it contains ':', it throws invalidTimestamp (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:~150-160). The whole file is rejected as invalid; for LRCLIB the try? makes it a silent 'No lyrics found'. Serialize followed by re-parse in the editor fails the same way for any lyric text starting with such a bracket.

scenario: A watched-folder LRC or LRCLIB row has [offset:inf], a minutes field of 1e300 or 'inf' (Swift Double accepts 'inf', 'infinity', 'nan'), then the user opens Edit Lyrics and presses Save Copy or Export.
expected: Non-finite or out-of-range numbers fail the parse as invalid; saving never traps.
actual_by_code: parseTimestamp and the offset tag use TimeInterval(String) with only >= 0 and < 60 checks (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:~205-215, 73-78). Serialize then does Int((offset*1000).rounded()) (:114) and Int((max(0,time)*100).rounded()) (:217), which trap for inf or values above Int.max. Editor save and export both call serialize (LocalLyricsEditor.swift:33,53).

scenario: Hostile LRC: one multi-megabyte line carrying 100k ascending stamps ([00:01][00:02]...), or several hundred thousand lines, from LRCLIB's community uploads or a synced folder.
expected: The parser enforces limits (bytes, lines, stamps per line, text length) so one record cannot hang the UI or balloon memory.
actual_by_code: parse has no cap; each stamp appends a pending row (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:89-95) and OnlineLyrics decodes the whole response with URLSession.shared.data, unbounded (OnlineLyrics.swift:119-133). Lyrics stage and lock card render every line; Copy All joins them all. Local files use String(contentsOf:) with no size check on the main actor (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:164,269).
existing_test: none (LyricAccuracyLabParseTests is a corpus accuracy lab, not a fuzz or limit test)

scenario: User adds ~ or / as a Lyrics Folder, or a sync client holds a folder with a 2 GB .lrc.
expected: Folder indexing is bounded, off the main thread, and skips oversized files.
actual_by_code: init calls rescanFolders() synchronously on the main actor (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:~145-160), which walks the folder recursively with fileManager.enumerator (:255-262) and reads each *.lrc fully (:269). No depth, count or size limit; folder events trigger the same walk after 150 ms (:575-595). F-043 notes the main-thread cost but not the unbounded input.

scenario: Lyric text from LRCLIB or a local file contains bidi overrides (U+202E), zero-width characters, control characters or enormous lines, then it is drawn, copied, or returned by the Get Current Lyric intent.
expected: Lyric lines are normalised (controls and bidi stripped, length capped) like Now Playing strings.
actual_by_code: Now Playing text is filtered and capped at 512 scalars (NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:55-63). LocalLyricsDocument.parse keeps line text verbatim (:122-123), and CurrentLyricIntent returns shown.line.text as-is (IslaIntents.swift:119). Copy Line and Copy All carry the raw characters.

scenario: The Get Current Lyric or Get Current Track result is piped into a user's Shortcut that runs a shell script, AppleScript or URL.
expected: Documented as untrusted text, or sanitised/length-capped before it leaves the app.
actual_by_code: Both intents return raw strings (IslaIntents.swift:119,138); lyric text originates from anyone who can publish to LRCLIB, and track titles from any now-playing app. No description warns the Shortcuts author (IslaIntents.swift:97,126).

scenario: Siri, Spotlight or a Stream Deck runs Get Current Track, Get Current Lyric, Play or Pause, Next or Previous while the Mac is locked.
expected: Intents that read or act on media require unlock (authenticationPolicy) or are refused like the hot keys are.
actual_by_code: None of the eight intents sets authenticationPolicy and none checks LockScreenPresence.isLocked; perform() calls straight into the model (IslaIntents.swift:69-206). The hot key path is refused while locked, the intents are not, so someone at a locked Mac can read the track, read the lyric line, and skip or pause via Siri.

scenario: Set Lyric Delay receives NaN or a huge value (a Shortcut variable that does not coerce to a number).
expected: Non-finite values are rejected or clamped to 0.
actual_by_code: userOffset's didSet computes min(max(userOffset,-3),3) (LyricsStore.swift:42-47); with NaN, Swift's min/max return NaN, the NaN is stored and written to defaults (:49), and every lyric position becomes NaN so comparisons all fail and the stage stops following. Whether Shortcuts can deliver NaN to a Double parameter with inclusiveRange was not verified.

scenario: A local process posts the unauthenticated distributed notification com.apple.screenIsUnlocked while the Mac is really locked, or screenIsLocked while unlocked.
expected: Isla confirms the transition against CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary (CGSSessionScreenIsLocked) before changing state.
actual_by_code: LockScreenPresence.handleLock/handleUnlock trust the notification by name alone (LockScreenPresence.swift:30-66; no CGSession call anywhere in Sources). A forged unlock drops the lock card and re-enables hot keys, intents and clipboard polling during a real lock; a forged lock puts a controls-bearing card (transport, volume, output, Liked heart) on an unlocked desktop and stops clipboard polling.

scenario: A local process posts forged com.spotify.client.PlaybackStateChanged broadcasts with crafted 'Playback Position' and 'Name'.
expected: Forged announcements cannot desynchronise lyrics or hold the display.
actual_by_code: applySpotifyBroadcast trusts note.userInfo (MediaController.swift:395, 417-454). Finite, in-range positions re-anchor the clock; a differing Name puts the controller into beginAwaitingTrackChange, which holds readings. Sanity checks exist for non-finite and out-of-range positions (:444-445) but sender identity is not checked (object: nil).

scenario: With Hide from Screen Recording on (default), the user screen-shares and opens Quick Look on a Shelf card, the AirDrop sheet, Import LRC or Add Folder open panels, Save panel, or the About panel.
expected: Either those windows are also excluded or the setting states it covers the island panel only.
actual_by_code: Only NotchPanel sets sharingType = .none (NotchPanel.swift:163-168; grep finds no other sharingType). QLPreviewPanel, NSSharingService sheets, NSOpenPanel/NSSavePanel and the About panel are system or AppKit windows with default sharing, so file contents and names are captured. The setting row says only 'Hide from Screen Recording' (Localizable.strings:65).

scenario: Headphones moment for a Bluetooth device whose name is localised or not in the English possessive form ('Наушники Эльшода', 'AirPods Max — Эльшод', 'Elshod AirPods').
expected: The owner's name never appears on the pill, in either shipped locale.
actual_by_code: shortName only splits on "'s " and "’s " (AmbientWatch.swift:171-179) and otherwise returns the full device name, which is shown on the island for 2.2 s. Russian is a shipped locale, and Russian possessives have no apostrophe.

scenario: Check what Isla persists about listening: online lyric lookups, local bindings, timing nudges.
expected: Settings offers a way to clear every listening-derived store, and the README says what is kept; turning Look Up Online off clears or stops growing the cache.
actual_by_code: OnlineLyricsCache writes lyrics-online/cache.json: up to 1000 entries keyed title|artist|album|duration plus the lyric lines, and misses for 14 days (OnlineLyrics.swift:290-420), as plaintext default-permission JSON, loaded at launch regardless of the switch. No Settings action clears it (only Clear Imported Lyrics and bindings exist). Uninstall docs (README.md:96-99) list Application Support but not ~/Library/Preferences/com.ctimothe.isla.plist, Caches or Cookies.

scenario: Shelf Clear / uninstall: what file names and paths remain in defaults.
expected: Clearing the Shelf leaves no file names; leftover state is documented.
actual_by_code: persist() rewrites shelf.urls, .bookmarks and .dates on every change (ShelfStore.swift:407-435), so Clear empties them. But RecordingPickup keeps up to 1000 met file names in recordings.seen (RecordingPickup.swift:44-53, ShelfStore.swift:166-167) and nothing clears them on Clear, on Clear Screenshots Folder, or on uninstall. Names of user-renamed captures persist even after the files are trashed.

scenario: Drag a Mail attachment, Photos item or browser image onto the island, then double-click the card.
expected: A file that arrived by promise from untrusted content keeps its quarantine flag so Gatekeeper still assesses it when opened from the Shelf.
actual_by_code: Promised files are written to Application Support/Dropped/<uuid> by NSFilePromiseReceiver (NotchRootView.swift:~262-282, AppPaths.swift:45-57) and Open calls NSWorkspace.shared.open(item.url) (ShelfStore.swift:407-409) with no extended-attribute check or stamp. Whether the providing app sets com.apple.quarantine on promise output is source-dependent and not verified, and Isla never adds it.

scenario: A promise source writes a huge or endless file, or a drag offers thousands of promises.
expected: Per-drop and total size are bounded and the disk fill is visible.
actual_by_code: receivePromisedFiles has no size limit; the Dropped folder is pruned only at launch and only by age (AppPaths.swift:62-72), so a single session can fill the disk, and an open promise holds an NSFileCoordination read on a background queue indefinitely (NotchRootView.swift:~262-282).

scenario: Opt-in Save Clipboard Screenshots is on and a copied image or movie is large or malformed: a TIFF whose header claims 60000x60000, or movie bytes of several GB.
expected: Image and movie bytes from the pasteboard are size- and dimension-capped before decode or write.
actual_by_code: movieData() reads pasteboard.data(forType:) for any movie-conforming type synchronously on the main actor with no cap (ClipboardStore.swift:202,231-239), then saveMovie writes it. TIFF goes through NSBitmapImageRep(data:)...representation(using: .png) on a global queue with no dimension check (:280-282). Gated by the opt-in switch, but Universal Clipboard delivers data from other devices.

scenario: Copy a very large string (hundreds of MB) with history on.
expected: The size is checked before the string is materialised.
actual_by_code: pollNow calls pasteboard.string(forType: .string) on the main actor and only afterwards trims and caps to 256 KiB (ClipboardStore.swift:215-217, 258-261), so the full string is read and bridged first, stalling the panel and pointer sampler. The ledger covers the 256 KB cap, not the read cost.

scenario: macOS 26/27 'Paste from Other Apps' pasteboard privacy: the OS prompts or denies programmatic reads of the general pasteboard by apps that do not paste on user action.
expected: Isla detects NSPasteboard accessBehavior, uses detectPatterns/changeCount-only probing, or explains the state in Settings.
actual_by_code: No use of accessBehavior, detectPatterns or any access-denied handling (grep of Sources). The poll reads .string, .readObjects, .png/.tiff directly every 0.5 s after a change (ClipboardStore.swift:174-218). Behaviour on a macOS version that prompts, silently returns nil, or throttles cannot be settled from code; history could appear empty with no explanation.

scenario: Lock-screen card used by someone with physical access to a locked Mac.
expected: The card exposes only what the owner accepts, and state-changing controls are opt-in; each is listed in checklist.md (CLAUDE.md hard constraint).
actual_by_code: Beyond the Liked Songs heart (decision 12), the card also switches the system default output device, sets output volume and seeks lyrics (LockScreenCard.swift via AudioOutputs.swift:258-307 and SystemVolume), with no authentication. Show on Lock Screen is on by default, and the track title, artist and lyrics are visible to anyone passing a locked Mac.

scenario: Spotify AppleScript track-id lookup and catalogue call run for every Spotify track even when Show Lyrics is off and no account is connected.
expected: A capability that has no enabled consumer does not run, and does not raise the macOS Automation prompt.
actual_by_code: On every track or player change, requestSpotifyTrackID runs unconditionally when Spotify is shown (MediaController.swift:1431-1433), sending an Apple event to Spotify and triggering the one-time Automation consent (documented at :610-622). When connected, trackMetadata then calls GET /v1/tracks/{id} per track, and per the inventory nothing reads the result. No lyrics or heart setting gates either.

scenario: Isla ships with no privacy manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) although it uses required-reason APIs (UserDefaults, ProcessInfo.systemUptime, file timestamps, getxattr, sysctl) and makes network requests.
expected: A manifest declares API reasons and collected-data types, or the decision not to ship one is recorded.
actual_by_code: No PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in the repo; Scripts/bundle.sh assembles Info.plist and resources without one. Diagnostics reads getxattr and sysctl (Diagnostics.swift:171-190). Not required for a notarised direct download today, so this is a documentation gap.

scenario: The app is unsandboxed, hardened-runtime, with only the Apple Events entitlement, and parses untrusted data in-process: LRC text, LRCLIB JSON, artwork images, MyMemory JSON, pasteboard TIFF.
expected: A decision is recorded that parsers run with full user privileges, or risky parsers are isolated.
actual_by_code: Resources/Isla.entitlements has no com.apple.security.app-sandbox; ImageIO decode and JSON parse happen in the main process. Hardened runtime without disable-library-validation is correct and is the only isolation present.

scenario: Any same-user process runs defaults write com.ctimothe.isla to flip privacy-relevant switches (translateOnline, onlineLyrics, hideFromCapture, spotifyClientID) or sets DI_* variables through launchctl setenv.
expected: Network-reaching and capture-exposing switches are tamper-evident or the trust model is documented.
actual_by_code: All switches are plain UserDefaults (NotchViewModel.swift:895-905, SpotifyAccount.swift:162-166); the client id override has no Settings UI and no integrity check. DebugTrail reads DI_* once at launch (DebugTrail.swift:19-31).

scenario: DebugTrail is armed (DI_MEDIA, DI_GEOM or DI_OPEN_LYRICS set in the launch environment).
expected: Trail output goes to a private path, is created 0600 without following symlinks, and omits titles.
actual_by_code: note() appends to the fixed, world-readable /tmp/di-debug.log (DebugTrail.swift:33-45) via FileHandle(forWritingTo:), which follows a pre-planted symlink, and the lines include track titles (MediaPane.swift:114) and lyric state. Off by default, so only a launchctl-set environment exposes it.

scenario: Copy Diagnostics report is pasted into a public GitHub issue; logs contain error text marked .public.
expected: No public-marked message can contain a path, user name or file name.
actual_by_code: Most paths use .private for localizedDescription, but several log localizedDescription publicly: launch-at-login failure (SettingsPane.swift:642), update check failure (UpdateCheck.swift:74), helper write failure (NowPlayingFeed.swift:413). SMAppService and file errors can quote the bundle path (for example /Users/<name>/Applications). Redaction of the rest depends on OSLogStore returning <private> for the current process (DiagnosticsTests.testTheLogIsReadBackWithPrivateValuesRedacted) and holds only without a private-data logging profile installed.

scenario: Local lyrics index.json (or a migrated v4/v5 index) is edited so a stored document path contains '..' and the user presses Clear Imported Lyrics.
expected: Deletion is limited to files inside the imports directory after path standardisation.
actual_by_code: clearImportedDocuments checks document.path.hasPrefix(importsDirectory.path + "/") then removeItem(atPath:) (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:~327-335); the prefix test is on the raw string, so '<imports>/../../x' passes and deletes an arbitrary user file. Requires write access to the owner's index.json, so exposure is local-only.

scenario: CI supply chain for the public repo: build.yml uses third-party actions and runs ./scripts/check on pull_request.
expected: Actions pinned to commit SHAs, token permissions minimised, release secrets unavailable to PR runs.
actual_by_code: .github/workflows/build.yml uses actions/checkout@v5 and actions/upload-artifact@v7 by tag, with no permissions: block and no SHA pin; the workflow runs repo-controlled scripts on PRs. Signing identities are release-owner inputs and not in CI, which limits the blast radius.

scenario: Quarantine and Gatekeeper behaviour for the helper in a quarantined or translocated copy: user runs from the DMG, a Downloads folder, or an AppTranslocation path.
expected: Isla detects translocation and the refused load and says so; the dylib is not loaded from a randomised read-only path unnoticed.
actual_by_code: Quarantine is diagnosed (Diagnostics.swift:186-190) and a refused load exits with status 3 and a Settings explanation (NowPlayingFeed.swift:245-258). Bundle.main.path under an AppTranslocation mount resolves to the translocated path, which perl can load; no translocation detection exists in Sources.

scenario: OnlineLyrics identity with a huge or non-finite duration (player reports duration above 9.2e18 s, or Infinity from the AppleScript fallback).
expected: The duration is validated as finite and within a sane range before it is formatted.
actual_by_code: LyricsCoordinator only guards duration > 0 (LyricsCoordinator.swift:221). request(for:) and OnlineLyricsCache.key call Int(identity.duration.rounded()) (OnlineLyrics.swift:69,322), which traps on NaN, Infinity or values beyond Int.max. The helper JSON path cannot carry Infinity, so this needs a finite but absurd value or a non-JSON source.

scenario: Isla runs on the AppleScript fallback from launch (helper refused by Gatekeeper, or the route closed) with Spotify or Music playing, panel open, lyrics on.
expected: Shuffle and repeat show, the Spotify id resolves so the lock-card heart appears, the 1 Hz precision correction and Spotify broadcasts steer the clock, and lyric nudges are keyed to the real player.
actual_by_code: displayedPlayerPID is assigned only in apply() (MediaController.swift:1427) and clear() (:1726). refreshFromPlayers() (:1831-1861) sets activeApp, sourceName and track but never the pid. displayedPlayerApp (:600-603) is derived only from the pid, so it is nil in fallback. Consequences: refreshPlaybackModes nils shuffle and repeat (:531-535), precisionPlayer is nil (:591-595), receiveSpotifyBroadcast returns at its displayedPlayerIsSpotify guard (:416), requestSpotifyTrackID never runs (:624) so there is no heart, and lyricPlayerID is 'other' (:608-610). checklist.md:24-36 says refusing consent costs those controls but does not say the fallback itself loses them.

scenario: A transport tap (pause, next) is made while the helper is down between a crash and its 2 s restart, then the helper comes back up.
expected: The held command reaches the player once the replacement helper is up, as the comment at NowPlayingFeed.swift:312-315 promises.
actual_by_code: launch() writes pendingCommand immediately after task.run() (NowPlayingFeed.swift:300, 316-319), so the line is already in the pipe before perl has loaded the dylib. In helper.m the constructor starts the feed thread and the command reader together (:523-524); the reader's fgets returns at once and handleCommand returns silently while sFeedReady is still false (:373). sFeedReady is set only after dlopen and dlsym finish (:443). The replayed command is very likely dropped, and the optimistic icon reverts after PlaybackIntent's 1.5 s timeout.

scenario: Wake from sleep or Try Again while on the fallback, and the helper's first record is empty because MediaRemote is not ready yet. Spotify is playing.
expected: The fallback keeps showing the Spotify track until the helper delivers a real session.
actual_by_code: feedDelivered() treats any first snapshot as proof of life: it removes the fallback observers, sets feedAvailable and clears fallbackReason (MediaController.swift:1819-1829) before checking whether the snapshot is empty. receive() then calls admission(): an empty snapshot is kept only when holdsASong and displayedPlayerApp != nil (:1072-1074), and displayedPlayerApp is nil in fallback (see the fallback scenario). It returns .accept, apply() calls clear() (:1363, :1700-1750), and the island says nothing is playing with no fallback observers left until the next full helper record.

scenario: Get Current Lyric runs from a Shortcut, Stream Deck key or Focus automation while the panel is closed and a synced track is playing.
expected: Returns the line sung right now.
actual_by_code: CurrentLyricIntent reads model.media.position directly (IslaIntents.swift:108-113). The 10 Hz ticker runs only while the panel is open or locked (MediaController.swift:2065-2080; setActive at :491-523). While closed, position is rewritten only when a snapshot is adopted. The helper suppresses unchanged payloads for 5 s (helper.m:52, 108-112) and MediaRemote re-serves one elapsed/timestamp pair while playing. The value can therefore be about 5 s old, and the intent returns a line from several seconds ago with no extrapolation from the anchor.

scenario: The player re-describes the same song under another route: wake retry hands over from the AppleScript fallback to the helper, or the helper dies and the fallback takes over, while the panel is closed and the song keeps playing.
expected: No visible event. The track did not change.
actual_by_code: The two routes build different track keys: PlayerState.key is 'spotify|title|artist|album' (PlayerBridge.swift:46) and the feed's is 'pid|title|artist|album' (MediaController.swift:1397). The handover flips the key, so the sneak-peek sink fires (NotchController.swift:1064-1072) and the pill widens for 2.2 s. LyricsCoordinator sees a new logicalTrackKey, cancels lookups and re-resolves (LyricsCoordinator.swift:243-269). playerChanged also resets positionSettled and the playback intent (MediaController.swift:1435-1448). Artwork is blanked after 180 ms (:1608-1627) and re-requested at the next poll.

scenario: A late AppleScript state reply from the fallback lands just after the helper takes over (retry handover).
expected: Once feedAvailable is true, scripted readings stop writing to the display.
actual_by_code: refreshFromPlayers()'s completion (MediaController.swift:1832-1860) has no feedAvailable or retrying guard. A PlayerBridge.currentState call queued before the handover still assigns track (fallback-format key), isPlaying, duration, activeApp and calls adopt(). The next helper snapshot then flips the key back (apply, :1403-1430), so a second spurious new-track event follows (peek, lyric re-resolve, artwork blank).

scenario: A watched lyrics folder is deleted and recreated, renamed, or lives on an external disk or share that is unmounted and remounted, or was not mounted at launch.
expected: Dropping a new .lrc into it is picked up within 150 ms, as the folder-watcher contract says.
actual_by_code: installFolderWatchers() (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:572-587) runs only from startWatchingFolders (:378-382), addFolder (:194) and removeFolder (:205). It opens the directory with O_EVTONLY and skips the folder if open fails (:577-578), so a folder not mounted at launch never gets a watcher. A .delete or .rename event on the directory fd only schedules a rescan (:582, 589-596). The source stays bound to the dead inode and nothing reinstalls it, so the folder is never watched again until the app restarts or a folder is added or removed.

scenario: The user fixes timing in an existing .lrc inside a watched folder using an editor that writes in place, or drops lyrics into a subfolder of the watched folder.
expected: The new text is indexed within 150 ms and the playing track picks it up.
actual_by_code: The only watcher is a .write/.rename/.delete vnode source on the top-level directory descriptor (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:577-583). A directory descriptor reports entries added or removed, not content writes to an existing file or changes inside nested folders. rescanFolders does enumerate recursively (:254-261), but it runs only from watcher events, manual Rescan, add or remove folder, and launch. The stale document keeps matching and the edit is never seen.

scenario: Translate cover is on and the panel is open. The user clicks the dots to reveal the source, then copies a password elsewhere and presses the translate-clipboard hotkey, or the Translate service, without the panel folding.
expected: The incoming text arrives covered, since the reveal belonged to the previous text.
actual_by_code: The reveal key is the constant 'translate.source' (TranslatePane.swift:24-27; PrivacyMode.hides at PrivacyMode.swift:93-95). The hotkey handler (AppDelegate.swift:49-52) calls NotchController.translate (:541-574), which sets the input and calls setOpen(true) (a no-op on an open panel) but never touches PrivacyMode. revealed is cleared only in collapse() (NotchController.swift:1218; PrivacyMode.swift:121-126). The pasted secret shows in full in the source field, and the result column is never covered at all (F-002).

scenario: Translate holds typed text and an answer. The user leaves the tab and returns, or folds and reopens the panel, with the text unchanged.
expected: The answer already on screen is kept. Nothing is recomputed, and nothing is re-sent when Translate Online is on.
actual_by_code: The pane runs .task(id: translator.request) on every appearance (TranslatePane.swift:61). schedule() sleeps 320 ms and calls translator.translate() (:379-391) with no check that outputSource already equals the trimmed input (Translator.swift:407-459; outputSource set at :466). Each revisit re-runs the whole pipeline. For an online-only pair OnlineTranslation.translate re-sends every 480-character chunk to MyMemory (OnlineTranslation.swift:65-89), so folding mid-answer and reopening repeats the cost and re-sends the text off the Mac.

scenario: Typing an Uzbek or Kazakh sentence with Translate Online on, pausing more than 320 ms between words.
expected: Cost stays proportional to the final sentence, or the user is told that online translation is as-you-type.
actual_by_code: Every pause longer than 320 ms fires a request carrying the whole text so far (TranslatePane.swift:61, 387-390; Translator.translate :407-459), then the next keystroke cancels it client-side. A 200-character sentence typed in ten bursts sends about 10 prefixes of growing length. If MyMemory's anonymous allowance counts characters sent (not verified here), that burns it roughly quadratically. The failure then reads 'Today's free online translations are used up.' (Translator.swift:545-546). F-042 covers long pasted input, not per-pause prefixes.

scenario: On the full lyrics page the user scrolls ahead by hand (reading mode), then the song ends or is skipped while the page stays open.
expected: The next song's page starts following its own sung line again, or at least offers the Sync pill straight away.
actual_by_code: following is @State of LyricsStage (LyricsStage.swift:64) and is set to false by the wheel monitor (:290-296). It returns to true only from the Sync pill (:364) or a line tap (:417). MediaPane mounts LyricsStage without a track id (MediaPane.swift:83-100), so the state survives the track change. The new ScrollView's onAppear sets reading to line[anchor] (LyricsStage.swift:284), but following stays false, so the page stops tracking the voice and the pill appears only after the page drifts two lines (:302).

scenario: The user presses Import LRC for song A and sits in the open panel. The next song starts before they confirm the file.
expected: The file binds to song A, the song they were looking at when they pressed Import.
actual_by_code: chooseLocalLyricsFile runs panel.runModal() (NotchViewModel.swift:397-403) and only then calls lyricsCoordinator.importLocalFile (LyricsCoordinator.swift:194-198), which reads currentIdentity at that moment. After a track change that is song B. LocalLyricsLibrary.importDocument stores the binding under B's identity (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:168-181), a permanent wrong binding. Nothing captures the identity at button press.

scenario: A slow promised file (large iCloud Photos original, Mail attachment) finishes after the user has moved on, or after the Mac locked or the display slept.
expected: The card is added quietly. Nothing opens over a locked screen or a dark display.
actual_by_code: deliverPromised (NotchRootView.swift:328-335) calls onDrop, which runs vm.accept, pointer.setInside(true), setOpen(true) and scheduleCollapseIfPointerAway (NotchController.swift:865-873) with no lock, sleep or drag-state check. verdictForDeliberateOpen (NotchViewModel.swift:496-498) is not consulted. vm.accept also switches the tab to Shelf (NotchViewModel.swift:967-975). Over the shield this grows the click region from the locked pill rect to the open body, then the 0.6 s collapse recuts it for the unlocked layout. Unlocked, the panel pops open on whatever the user is doing.

scenario: A display change, wake, or Panel Width commit rebuilds the panel while a Mail or Photos file promise is still being fulfilled.
expected: The file still lands on the Shelf.
actual_by_code: receivePromisedFiles uses [weak self] on the NotchRootView (NotchRootView.swift:269). rebuild() sets rootView to nil and contentView to nil (NotchController.swift:763-795), deallocating the view. The pending-batch DispatchWorkItem (NotchRootView.swift:321-325) also holds it weakly. The file is written under AppPaths.dropInbox() but never added, and it is trashed at a later launch after 7 days (NotchStores.swift:80; F-019).

scenario: Rapid double tap on the lock-card Liked Songs heart (or a tap and an immediate re-tap after a track change).
expected: The last tap wins, on the server and on screen.
actual_by_code: Each tap spawns its own Task (SpotifyAccount.swift:392-421) with an optimistic write, then PUT or DELETE to the Web API, with no serialization. Two requests are in flight at once, and which one Spotify applies last is not controlled, so the server can end liked while the UI shows hollow. A failed first request rolls back with !wants (:415-417) regardless of the second tap.

scenario: Disconnect Spotify (or switch accounts) while a Liked-Songs lookup for the playing track is in flight.
expected: Nothing from the old account survives the disconnect.
actual_by_code: disconnect() clears saved and bumps credentialGeneration (SpotifyAccount.swift:290-297). refreshSavedState's Task has no generation or isConnected check after its await and writes saved[trackID] = flag (:347-379). The old account's answer lands after the clear. After a reconnect the guard saved[trackID] == nil (:348) skips refreshing, so the heart can show the previous account's liked state for that track until the track changes.

scenario: A tap is held while the helper restarts, the helper then fails to come back and the app falls back to scripting, and Try Again or a wake retry succeeds minutes or hours later.
expected: Held commands expire. A stale Next from hours ago is never replayed.
actual_by_code: write() stores the tap in pendingCommand when input is nil (NowPlayingFeed.swift:405, 416). The .fallback branch of handleTermination does not clear it (:351-353). Only stop() (:181) and launch() (:316-318) touch it, so a later retry's feed.start() reaches launch(), which replays the old line. There is no timestamp or TTL. The helper-side readiness race (see the replay scenario) may mask this today.

scenario: During a helper restart the user taps Pause and then clicks a lyric line (seek), or taps Next and then Pause.
expected: Both intents survive, or the UI does not claim the dropped one.
actual_by_code: pendingCommand is a single slot (NowPlayingFeed.swift:129, 405, 416). Each write while the helper is down overwrites the last, so the pause is lost while MediaController has already flipped isPlaying and the icon (:860-868). The icon reverts when PlaybackIntent's 1.5 s confirmation timeout expires (PlaybackIntent.swift:60-71).

scenario: The user presses Try Again or a wake retry fires while a restart delay from an earlier helper death is still pending.
expected: Exactly one helper process.
actual_by_code: handleTermination schedules launch() with asyncAfter (NowPlayingFeed.swift:355-357) and nothing cancels it. start() (:142-167) calls launch() directly, and launch() has no process == nil guard (:261-267). Both can run, overwriting process, input and output, orphaning the first helper; its terminationHandler then reaches handleTermination while process points at the second. The retry guards (MediaController.swift:1809-1815) make the window narrow.

scenario: Two clipboard screenshots are saved within the same second, for example a phone copy and a local one, with Save Clipboard Screenshots on.
expected: Both are kept, the second with a (2) suffix.
actual_by_code: ScreenshotVault.write picks the file name with a fileExists loop, then writes, all inside DispatchQueue.global(qos: .utility).async (ScreenshotVault.swift:115-136). The global queue is concurrent and there is no lock, so two writes starting together both see the same name free and both write it atomically. The second replaces the first, both completions return the same URL, and the shelf dedupes by URL. One capture is silently lost.

scenario: The user clicks a lyric line on the stage or lock card in the 50-700 ms between pressing Next and the new song's title arriving.
expected: The click is ignored or applies to the song the line belongs to.
actual_by_code: next() marks the track change as awaited (MediaController.swift:870-874) but seek(to:) has no check of isAwaitingTrackChange (:962-984). It clamps to the old duration, sets the anchor and a pendingSeek, and sends feed.seek to the displayed pid, which already plays the new song. The new song jumps to the old song's line time. While pendingSeek is set, the new track's first readings are discarded until the 1.5 s expiry (judgeSeekReading, :165-195), so the new title shows the old position.

scenario: The user drags the scrubber (panel or lock card) and the track changes before release, for example at a natural end of song while dragging near the end.
expected: The drag is cancelled, or the seek still targets the song being dragged.
actual_by_code: onEnded recomputes media.duration * fraction at release (MediaPane.swift:350-361; LockScreenCard.swift:650-653) from whatever song now plays. The scrubbing state holds only a fraction, not a track key, so the seek lands at the same percentage of the new song, which can be its last seconds.

scenario: Ten or more skips per second (a held key or a Stream Deck macro) with the panel open while Spotify is shown.
expected: The bar and lyrics resume ticking cleanly once the storm ends. During it nothing starves.
actual_by_code: Every apply() ends in updateTicker() (MediaController.swift:1579), which invalidates and re-creates the 0.1 s repeating timer (:2057-2080). Each command makes the helper emit a record plus a forced echo at 0.35 s (helper.m:401-411), and each Spotify broadcast asks for a fresh report now and 0.3 s later (MediaController.swift:1130-1137). Snapshots can arrive faster than the 100 ms interval, so the new timer is replaced before it first fires and tick() does not run. The bar freezes for the storm, then recovers. Each skip also queues a stale Spotify id AppleScript (separate scenario).

scenario: Pause Spotify from its own window or a media key with the panel open and lyrics on. Spotify's pause broadcast arrives before MediaRemote's paused snapshot.
expected: The paused bar and lyric stand at the player's true position.
actual_by_code: receiveSpotifyBroadcast anchors the clock at the exact position (MediaController.swift:415-451, 762-766) while isPlaying is still true, so tick() keeps extrapolating forward (:2084-2091). When the paused snapshot arrives, adopt() treats a backwards delta under 2 s as a rebase that keeps the displayed (ahead) value (:2047-2054). precisionSteers also skips MediaRemote's position (:1512-1543). The immediate precisionCorrect() (:765) fixes it only if its reply lands after isPlaying flips. If it lands first, the playing-branch rule for deltas in (-1,0) is rebase only (:832-853). The paused clock can sit 0.05-0.3 s ahead, and a resume carries that offset onward.

scenario: Overlapping helper publishes: a MediaRemote notification and the 2 s poll start two records a few milliseconds apart, with a pause landing between them.
expected: Records reach the app in the order the states happened.
actual_by_code: publishSnapshot chains getIsPlaying, getInfo and an async confirmOwner hop per record on one serial queue (helper.m:223-313, 317-344). Two overlapping chains interleave, so the older chain can finish and emit last. Snapshots carry no sequence number, and for a playing record describesAMomentAlreadyPast returns false (MediaController.swift:1919-1937). The stale 'playing' record can flip a paused UI back until the next differing poll, up to 2-5 s because of dedupe and heartbeat (helper.m:108-112).

scenario: The Mac sleeps for hours while a session is still marked playing, and wakes with the helper re-serving the pre-sleep elapsed/timestamp pair.
expected: The position resumes near where playback froze.
actual_by_code: The anchor uses the monotonic clock, which does not advance in sleep (MediaController.swift:124, 2086). reportedPosition ages a playing reading by Date() minus the MediaRemote timestamp (:1877-1893), and the wall clock does include sleep. If a player stays 'playing' across sleep without publishing a new pair, a snapshot right after wake is aged by the whole sleep and clamped to the duration. Whether Spotify, Music or browsers do that cannot be told from code.

scenario: A setOpen(true) caller runs in the same run-loop pass after a setOpen(false), for example a drop or keyboard claim landing right behind a walk-away close.
expected: The panel ends up open.
actual_by_code: setOpen(false) defers the isOpen change to the next pass (NotchController.swift:1187-1192) and bumps openGeneration only afterwards. A same-pass setOpen(true) returns at guard vm.isOpen != open (:1154) because isOpen is still true. It neither bumps openGeneration nor cancels the pending collapse, so the collapse runs and the open request is lost. toggle() works around it with a captured target (:678-684), but other callers do not.

scenario: Two copies are made within one 0.5 s poll (copy A then B, or a Universal Clipboard arrival right behind a local copy).
expected: Both land in history.
actual_by_code: ClipboardStore compares only the change counter every 0.5 s (0.2 s tolerance) and reads whatever is on the pasteboard then (ClipboardStore.swift:113-128, 174-176). The first copy is overwritten before it is read and never reaches history. This is not documented as a limit.

scenario: The user copies twice within 1.1 s (copy button, clipboard row tap), so two copy ticks overlap.
expected: The second tick shows its full duration.
actual_by_code: flash() raises the flag and always schedules a fixed 1.1 s lowering with no cancellation or token (Confirmation.swift:10-15). The first timer lowers the flag partway through the second tick. The comment at :5-8 acknowledges the trade, but a second flash is not extended.

scenario: A new clipboard entry, a Universal Clipboard arrival or a new Shelf card is inserted at the top while the pointer rests on a row's copy target or hover X.
expected: A click lands on the row the user was aiming at.
actual_by_code: ClipboardStore.record inserts at index 0 (ClipboardStore.swift:344-348) and ShelfStore.add inserts at the front and re-sorts (ShelfStore.swift:250-265). Rows are keyed by fresh ids, so the list shifts under a stationary pointer. A click made as the shift happens copies the wrong entry (and moves it to the top) or, with the hover X, removes the new item while the one meant for removal stays. The ledger covers deletion under a pointer, not insertion.

scenario: A Shelf card is held in a drag for more than 120 s, for example while spring-loaded folders open or the user is searching for the target.
expected: The panel stays open for the whole drag.
actual_by_code: ShelfDragSource.beginDragOut arms a 120 s DispatchWorkItem that clears isDraggingOut (ShelfDragSource.swift:113-134). A live drag past the limit loses its hold, so PointerWatcher.isDragging (NotchController.swift:948-950) goes false and the panel can fold under it, the failure the latch exists to prevent.

scenario: Import LRC or Add Lyrics Folder opens an NSOpenPanel with runModal() while the pointer leaves the panel.
expected: The panel stays up while its own dialog is up.
actual_by_code: runModal blocks the stack in NotchViewModel.chooseLocalLyricsFile and chooseLocalLyricsFolder (NotchViewModel.swift:397-413) while .common-mode timers keep running. MenuTracking holds the panel only for NSMenu tracking (MenuTracking.swift:19-73), not for modal panels. The pointer sampler can still fold the panel (and rebuild SwiftUI state) under a live modal. Whether the dialog also appears behind other apps (the app never activates) cannot be told from code.

scenario: Skip storm while Spotify is displayed: 10 track changes in one second.
expected: Only the final track's id lookup costs anything.
actual_by_code: Every apply() with a new key calls requestSpotifyTrackID (MediaController.swift:1430-1433), and each call enqueues a .background-priority AppleScript (PlayerBridge.swift:81-88). That priority never yields to later work (:481-490 only pollable scripts yield), so ten scripts run in order on the single serial queue. Replies for stale keys are discarded by the key guard (MediaController.swift:626-629) after the work is done. Any scripted transport (held song, fallback) queues behind them.

scenario: The panel is closed by a click while the pointer still rests on the island, then nothing moves the pointer.
expected: The hover edge returns, since the pointer is on the island.
actual_by_code: PointerWatcher reports hover only on change (PointerWatcher.swift:218-222). NotchController sets vm.isHovering = hovering && !vm.isOpen only inside that callback (:988-993). While open, hovering is true (hoverRect follows the open body) so isHovering is written false. After the close nothing flips wasHovering, so no callback runs and the island stays unlit until the pointer leaves and re-enters.

scenario: Quick Look and AirDrop are used on the Shelf in sequence, each opening a window Isla must activate for.
expected: When the last window closes, the keyboard goes back to the app that had it.
actual_by_code: ShelfSharing keeps one returnTo (ShelfSharing.swift:21-36). activateRemembering stores it only when the front app is not Isla (:25), and giveBackActivation clears it on the first close (:30-31). If Quick Look closes first, returnTo is nil when the AirDrop sheet finishes, so no hand-back happens and Isla stays active holding the keyboard, the hazard the file header describes.

scenario: AirDrop is chosen from a Shelf card, and nobody holds a reference to the NSSharingService.
expected: The didShare and didFail delegate calls fire so activation is handed back.
actual_by_code: airDrop() keeps the service only in a local variable (ShelfSharing.swift:50-58) and the delegate is the static AirDropDelegate. If AppKit does not retain the service while its picker is up, the callbacks that call giveBackActivation never arrive, which would leave Isla active (see the previous scenario). Not verifiable from code.

scenario: First-ever file drag onto the island on a fresh account, with Show Screen Captures on (the default) and Screenshot.app saving to the Desktop.
expected: Any permission prompt appears after the drag, with the Shelf on screen to explain it.
actual_by_code: draggingEntered calls onDragEntered (NotchRootView.swift:176-181), which runs vm.showShelfForDrag (NotchController.swift:849-858). That sets tab = .shelf (NotchViewModel.swift:1001-1006), whose didSet calls shelf.refreshFromDisk() (:87), and its first line is importNewRecordings (ShelfStore.swift:180-183, 216-229). That scans Desktop, Documents and Downloads on the main thread inside the drag callback. A first-time TCC prompt would block the main thread while the user is mid-drag and holding the mouse button.

scenario: Launch with a watched lyrics folder under Documents, Downloads or Desktop that this build has not yet been approved for.
expected: No prompt and no stall at launch, in line with the Shelf's no-file-access-at-launch rule.
actual_by_code: NotchController builds NotchStores as a property initializer (NotchController.swift:19-21). NotchStores.init creates LocalLyricsLibrary (NotchStores.swift:44), whose init runs rescanFolders() synchronously on the main thread (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:159, 208-297), enumerating the folder. installFolderWatchers opens it too (:577). A protected folder can raise a permission prompt that blocks launch with no panel to explain it. Whether a folder chosen through NSOpenPanel is exempt cannot be told from code.

scenario: Show Lyrics is switched off while an online lookup is in flight for the playing track.
expected: Nothing lyric-related continues. The in-flight request's answer is dropped and not cached.
actual_by_code: refreshVisibility calls reconcileTrack(force: true). Its isEnabled() == false branch (LyricsCoordinator.swift:221-230) resets state but does not cancel lookUpTask or bump lookUpGeneration, unlike the track-change path (:248-255). The task finishes, passes its generation guard (:306), calls onlineCache.remember (:307) and writes the answer to cache.json. Only publishAvailability then hides it. The inventory says nothing lyric-related runs while the switch is off.

scenario: Headphones connect while the island is hovered, the panel is open, or the display is still dark, then the user looks away.
expected: The connect moment still shows when the pointer leaves, or the refusal is not recorded as 'announced'.
actual_by_code: AmbientWatch records lastAnnounced and knownHeadphones before calling onEvent (AmbientWatch.swift:136-152). presentAmbient may then refuse for pointer, open panel or screensAsleep (NotchController.swift:1332-1351, 1377-1383), and the refusal is not reported back. The device is never announced again until it disconnects and the 30 s quiet window passes. The same applies to a charger plugged in during sleep. Moments are consumed even when refused.

scenario: The Panel Width slider is released: its action closure synchronously rebuilds the whole panel.
expected: A rebuild never destroys the view that is running the callback.
actual_by_code: commitBodyWidth runs inside the slider's onEditingChanged and calls AppDelegate.refreshGeometry (SettingsPane.swift:718-722), which calls rebuild() (NotchController.swift:583-585, 763-795). rebuild sets panel.contentView to nil, deallocating the hosting view whose gesture is still on the stack. The Settings tab is restored but its @State (armed confirmations, hover, scroll) resets. Whether the teardown inside the SwiftUI callback is safe cannot be told from code.

scenario: Caps Lock is on (common for Uzbek and Russian typists, and for anyone who leaves it latched) and the user presses Cmd-V, Cmd-C, Cmd-A, Cmd-X or Cmd-Z in the Translate source field.
expected: The panel's hand-rolled edit shortcuts work whatever the Caps Lock, Fn or numeric-pad flags are; compare with contains(.command) and no control/option, not equality.
actual_by_code: NotchPanel.swift:104 masks flags with .deviceIndependentFlagsMask, which includes .capsLock; :105 demands flags.subtracting(.shift) == .command exactly, so [.command,.capsLock] returns nil and the key falls through to super.sendEvent (:100). An accessory app has no Edit menu (comment :54-58), so nothing else handles it. Paste into Translate, the main flow, is dead while Caps Lock is on. No test mentions capsLock.

scenario: Hearing safety: any single click, tap or Switch Control tap on the lock-card volume bar, or a tremor press that lands near its right end, while headphones are on.
expected: A press must not change the system volume to an absolute value on mouse-down; commit on release or move toward the target in bounded steps, so a stray press cannot jump 0 to 100 percent.
actual_by_code: LockScreenCard.swift:713-720 uses DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) and calls SystemVolume.set(next) from the first onChanged event, with next = x/width. SystemVolume.swift:23-27 only clamps to 0...1. No ramp, no release-commit, no cap. The seek bar, by contrast, commits on release (:650-653).

scenario: VoiceOver, Switch Control or Voice Control user opens the panel through the compact island's accessibility action (it opens pinned) and now needs to close it.
expected: An accessible way to close: a labelled Close control or an .accessibilityAction(.escape) on the panel; the pin must also end by AT-driven focus changes, not only by mouse clicks.
actual_by_code: Pinned by NotchViewModel.swift:200 (isPinnedOpen = !pointerIsOnPanel, false for AX presses). The only exits are the same hot key, a real mouse click in another app (NotchController.swift:737-739 monitors leftMouseDown/rightMouseDown only), Space change, sleep or lock. The header close strip is a bare .onTapGesture (NotchContentView.swift:498-499) with no button trait or action; Escape never reaches a non-key panel (F-004 covers only the keyboard side). No accessibilityAction(.escape) anywhere in Sources.

scenario: A keyboard, VoiceOver, Switch Control or Voice Control user changes the Panel Width or Hover Delay slider by stepping it (arrow keys, VO increment, Voice Control 'increase').
expected: Every change, by any input, persists and takes effect; the width rebuild and the sampler retune must not depend on a pointer drag ending.
actual_by_code: Both sliders write only @State while moving (SettingsPane.swift:699-707, 727-729) and commit solely from onEditingChanged(false) (:131-136 and :98-103 into commitBodyWidth :718 and commitHoverDelay :731). Whether SwiftUI fires onEditingChanged for accessibility increments is not shown anywhere; if it does not, the value appears to move and is lost. The Lyric Delay slider writes through its binding directly (:299) and is not affected.

scenario: Voice-only or blind user asks Siri 'What is playing in Isla', 'Current lyric in Isla' or 'What line is this in Isla'.
expected: Siri speaks the answer (a dialog on the result); an empty answer says why ('No lyric yet').
actual_by_code: IslaIntents.swift:119 and :132 return .result(value:) with no dialog. CurrentLyricIntent returns the empty string for no lyrics and for the intro (:106, :117) with nothing spoken to tell them apart. No ProvidesDialog anywhere in the file. Whether Siri reads a bare string value is unverified.

scenario: Accessibility Keyboard (on-screen), Switch Control typing or a head pointer user types into Translate, so the pointer rests on the on-screen keyboard outside the panel.
expected: While the Translate field holds the keyboard and has text, a parked pointer does not fold the panel; folding waits for the keyboard handback.
actual_by_code: setKeyboard (NotchController.swift:1121-1141) says a field with text does not hold the panel open. PointerWatcher.swift:251-261 closes 0.32 s after the pointer leaves closeRect whatever the key state; isDragging counts only drags and menus (NotchController.swift:945-947). The fold sets wantsKeyboard false (:1187) and the next keystrokes go to the app underneath. Backlog decision 16 accepts this for mouse users, but for on-screen-keyboard users the pointer is necessarily away.

scenario: A podcast episode (Apple Podcasts is on the Music Only allowlist) plays, lyrics on, Look Up Lyrics Online on; a deaf or hard-of-hearing user wants captions.
expected: Spoken-word sessions skip lyric lookup (no episode title sent to LRCLIB) and say 'No lyrics for spoken audio'; a transcript or caption path is at least named as absent.
actual_by_code: MediaSourcePolicy.swift:36 admits com.apple.podcasts. LyricsCoordinator.swift:221 gates only on isEnabled, a non-empty title and duration > 0, so an episode runs the local match and the online search with title, show as artist, album and length. No spoken-word check (grep for podcast finds only comments). The result is 'No lyrics found.'. No caption or transcript code exists.

scenario: Voice Control or Switch Control point-scanning clicks a spot on the island or panel without first moving the real pointer there.
expected: The click reaches the panel; the window must accept events wherever an assistive click lands, not only where the sampler last saw the cursor.
actual_by_code: panel.ignoresMouseEvents is flipped only by the sampler from NSEvent.mouseLocation (PointerWatcher.swift:205, NotchController.swift:984-987), idle at 8 Hz. A synthesized mouse event at a point with the cursor elsewhere hits a click-through window and goes to the app underneath (the menu bar item behind the notch). The code only anticipates this for the AX action (NotchController.swift:640-647). Whether Voice Control or Switch Control move the cursor first is not shown.

dimension: accessibility and input combinations (beyond F-001..F-055 and the 435-scenario ledger)
scenario: VoiceOver, Switch Control or Voice Control scrolls the lyric stage to read ahead (AX scroll action, not a wheel event), then the song moves to the next line.
expected: Any user-driven scroll, by any input, stops the page following; the page does not yank back.
actual_by_code: Only ScrollWheelWatch (ScrollWheelWatch.swift:28-35, a local scrollWheel monitor) sets following = false (LyricsStage.swift:290-296). An AX scroll or scroll-to-visible changes scrollPosition without a wheel event, so following stays true and the next anchor change calls center(on:) (:277-279), dragging the page back. Same cause leaves VO moving to an off-screen line in the LazyVStack (:243) fighting the auto-scroll.

scenario: Output device without a main volume control (many USB DACs, HDMI) and the user relies on Accessibility > Audio > Balance for one-sided hearing; they touch the lock-card volume bar.
expected: The write preserves the left/right ratio the user set.
actual_by_code: SystemVolume.swift:30-33 writes the same scalar to channel 1 and 2; current() averages them (:12-24). The comment treats imbalance as drift to correct. A balance expressed as unequal channel volumes is silently flattened on first touch. Devices with a main element are unaffected.

scenario: Edit Lyrics sheet is open and the user types with the keyboard (or Voice Control dictation) while the pointer is parked in the lower part of the sheet or away from it.
expected: The panel does not fold under an open sheet and discard unsaved edits.
actual_by_code: The sheet (MediaPane.swift:116-127) has minHeight 340 (LocalLyricsEditorView.swift:116) against a 208 pt body (NotchMetrics.swift:15) and a 12 pt hover margin (NotchGeometry.swift:378-385). isDragging covers drags and menus only (NotchController.swift:945-947), not sheets. Whether the sheet sits inside hoverRect is not shown; if not, PointerWatcher.swift:251-261 folds the panel and the draft with it.

dimension: accessibility and input combinations (beyond F-001..F-055 and the 435-scenario ledger)
scenario: A VoiceOver or Voice Control user types in Translate and waits for the result, or the translation fails or finishes while they are on another control.
expected: The arrival of the result, the 'Translating...' state and the failure are announced (live region or announcement).
actual_by_code: TranslatePane.swift:133-200 swaps plain Text views for output, failure and the spinner row with no accessibility notification; Sources has no announcement API at all (F-013 lists other moments, not this one). The user must re-navigate to the right column to learn anything happened.

actual_by_code: Copy swaps the glyph to a checkmark (ClipboardPane.swift:66-68, Confirmation.swift:34-37); armed swaps the title and, in rows, the glyph (Confirmation.swift:78-80, 118-125); heart changes fill (LockScreenCard.swift:845); modes add a dot (ModeToggle.swift:27-35); selected output adds weight (LockScreenCard.swift:582) plus F-053's tint. Differentiate Without Color is never read, but no colour-only status was found.

dimension: accessibility and input combinations (beyond F-001..F-055 and the 435-scenario ledger)

actual_by_code: Equalizer cycles at about 1 to 1.35 Hz in a 10 pt box (Skeleton.swift:~150, durations 0.37 to 0.48 s autoreversed); skeleton shimmer 1.15 s (Skeleton.swift:30-35); spoiler dust twinkles per dot at under 0.6 Hz with random phases (SpoilerField.swift:90-95). All stop under Reduce Motion. No app-level motion control exists apart from the system setting.

No code reads buttonNumber or mouse button identity (grep), so the system swap applies throughout.
